## 󠀁[cache, cached, caching](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cache-cached-caching)󠁿

Use _cache_ as a noun or verb. Use _cached_ as a verb or adjective. Use _caching_
without an _e_ as a noun or verb.

## 󠀁[calendar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#calendar)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use _schedule, list_, or a contextually appropriate
verb.

## 󠀁[call back, callback](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#call-back-callback)󠁿

Use two words as a verb. Use one word as an adjective or noun.

## 󠀁[call out, callout](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#call-out-callout)󠁿

Use two words as a verb. Use one word as an adjective or noun.

## 󠀁[can](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#can)󠁿

Use _can_ to convey permission, to refer to an optional action, or to refer to a
possible outcome.

**Examples**

 **Recommended:** You can also use the slash command to insert a blockBlock Block
is the abstract term used to describe units of markup that, composed together, form
the content or layout of a webpage using the WordPress editor. The idea combines
concepts of what in the past may have achieved with shortcodes, custom HTML, and
embed discovery into a single consistent API and user experience..

 **Recommended:** The process can take up to 15 minutes.

See also [may](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#may).

## 󠀁[cancel, canceled, canceling, cancellation](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cancel-canceled-canceling-cancellation)󠁿

Use one _l_ for the verb _cancel_ and its other forms such as _canceled_ and _canceling_.

Use two _l_s for _cancellation_.

## 󠀁[capability](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#capability)󠁿

Avoid using in the context of features or functionalities of software or hardware.
Instead, rewrite the sentence without using the term.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** GutenbergGutenberg The Gutenberg project is the new Editor
Interface for WordPress. The editor improves the process and experience of creating
new content, making writing rich content much simpler. It uses ‘blocks’ to add richness
rather than shortcodes, custom HTML etc. [https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/](https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/)
has the capability of blockBlock Block is the abstract term used to describe units
of markup that, composed together, form the content or layout of a webpage using
the WordPress editor. The idea combines concepts of what in the past may have achieved
with shortcodes, custom HTML, and embed discovery into a single consistent API and
user experience. editing.

 **Recommended:** You can edit blocks with GutenbergGutenberg The Gutenberg project
is the new Editor Interface for WordPress. The editor improves the process and experience
of creating new content, making writing rich content much simpler. It uses ‘blocks’
to add richness rather than shortcodes, custom HTML etc. [https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/](https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/).

## 󠀁[carry out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#carry-out)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _run_ or _execute_.

See also [run](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#run).

## 󠀁[catalog](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#catalog)󠁿

Use instead of _catalogue_.

## 󠀁[cell phone, cellular phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cell-phone-cellular-phone)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _mobile_ or _mobile phone_, or if you’re talking about more
than phones, then use _mobile device_. It’s OK to just use _phone_ by itself when
the context is clear.

See also [mobile, mobile device, mobile phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#mobile-mobile-device-mobile-phone).

## 󠀁[cellular data](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cellular-data)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _mobile data_.

## 󠀁[cellular network](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cellular-network)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _mobile network_.

## 󠀁[CGI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cgi)󠁿

Initialism for _Common Gateway Interface_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[chapter](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#chapter)󠁿

Don’t use when referring to documentation that isn’t in the form of a book. Instead,
refer to documents, pages, or sections.

## 󠀁[character](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#character)󠁿

Use in reference to what a key on a keyboard stands for.

See also [symbol](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#symbol).

## 󠀁[chart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#chart)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb when referring to entering data for a chart. Instead, use _plot_.

## 󠀁[chat](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#chat)󠁿

Use as a noun only after identifying the context such as _audio chat_ or _video 
chat_ to avoid ambiguity.

It’s OK to use _chat_ as an adjective or verb.

## 󠀁[check](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#check)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb to refer to marking a checkbox. Instead, use _select_.

See also [checkbox](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#checkbox),
[clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#clear),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select).

## 󠀁[checkbox](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#checkbox)󠁿

One word. Not _check box_ or _check-box_.

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. If you have to use a descriptor, use _checkbox_.

For more information, see [Checkbox](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#checkbox).

See also [check](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#check).

## 󠀁[checksum](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#checksum)󠁿

One word. Not _check sum_ or _check-sum_.

## 󠀁[child folder](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#child-folder)󠁿

Don’t use. Use _subfolder, subdirectory, folder_, or the name of the folder.

See also [folder](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#folder).

## 󠀁[chip](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#chip)󠁿

Don’t use to mean _microprocessor_.

## 󠀁[chmod](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#chmod)󠁿

Contraction for _change mode_. Use lowercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[choose](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#choose)󠁿

Use _choose_ when referring to the action of the user making a choice from multiple
options, a list of items, or numerical values.

For more information, see [Choose](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#choose).

## 󠀁[clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#clear)󠁿

Use _clear_ as a verb when referring to the action of clearing a selection, usually
from a checkbox.

Use instead of _unselect, deselect,_ or _uncheck_.

For more information, see [Clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#clear).

See also [delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete),
[remove](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#remove).

## 󠀁[CLI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cli)󠁿

Initialism for _command line interface_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

For more information, see [Command-line syntax](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/).

## 󠀁[click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#click)󠁿

When the environment is presumably a desktop with a mouse, use _click_ to describe
the act of selecting most targets such as buttons, links, list items, and radio 
buttons or initiating an action by briefly pressing and releasing the mouse.

For more information, see [Click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#click).

See also [double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-click-double-click),
[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-tap-double-tap),
[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select), [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[client](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#client)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to a person. Instead, use _customer_.

See also [client/server](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#client-server).

## 󠀁[client/server](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#client-server)󠁿

Use a slash. Capitalize both words if the context requires _client_ to be capitalized.

See also [client](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#client).

## 󠀁[close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#close)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe closing applications, programs, files, documents, alerts,
and other UI elements.

For more information, see [Close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#close).

See also [open](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/#open), 
[end](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#end), [exit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#exit),
[interrupt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#interrupt),
[stop](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop).

## 󠀁[cloud](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cloud)󠁿

Don’t capitalize. In most cases, use _cloud_ as an adjective. Avoid using as a noun,
as in _the cloud_.

Don’t use cloud interchangeably with _internet_ or _web_.

## 󠀁[CMS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cms)󠁿

Initialism for _content management system_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[co-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#co)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _co-_ such as _coordinate, cooperate,_
and _coexist_, unless _co-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely necessary
to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[codebase](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#codebase)󠁿

One word. Not _code base_ or _code-base_.

## 󠀁[combo box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#combo-box)󠁿

Two words. It’s OK to use _combo box_ in developer documentation and for a technical
audience to describe a box in which the user can enter or select a value.

Avoid using in user documentation and for a general audience. Instead, refer to 
it as a _box_.

For more information, see [Dropdown list, combo box, and spin box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#dropdown-list-combo-box-and-spin-box).

## 󠀁[command](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. If you have to use a descriptor, use _command_.

It’s OK to use _item_ or _option_ in the context of commands.

For more information, see [Command-line syntax](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/).

See also [command line, command-line](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-line-command-line),
[command prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-prompt).

## 󠀁[command line, command-line](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-line-command-line)󠁿

Use two words as a noun. Hyphenate as an adjective.

Describe entering commands _at a command prompt_ not _on a command line_.

See also [command](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command),
[command prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-prompt).

## 󠀁[command prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-prompt)󠁿

Don’t use _command-line prompt, C prompt_, or _system prompt_.

Describe entering commands _at a command prompt_ not _on a command line_.

For more information, see [Command prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/#command-prompt).

See also [command](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command),
[command line, command-line](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#command-line-command-line).

## 󠀁[compile](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#compile)󠁿

It’s OK to use _compile_ as an adjective, as in _compile-time_, or as a verb. Don’t
use as a noun.

See also [compile time, compile-time](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#compile-time-compile-time).

## 󠀁[compile time, compile-time](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#compile-time-compile-time)󠁿

Use two words as a noun. Hyphenate as an adjective.

See also [compile](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#compile).

## 󠀁[comprise](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#comprise)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _is composed of, consists of, contains, includes_, or a 
contextually appropriate term.

## 󠀁[computer](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#computer)󠁿

Use to describe a computing device other than a mobile device.

Don’t use _mobile computer, portable computer, machine_, or _unit_.

See also [device](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#device),
[PC](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#pc).

## 󠀁[config](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#config)󠁿

Avoid using whenever possible. Instead, spell out the entire word in a non-code 
context such as _configuration_ or _configuring_. It’s OK to use _config_ when referring
to, for example, a data structure or a file with that name.

## 󠀁[connect](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#connect)󠁿

Don’t use _connect_ when you mean _plug in_.

## 󠀁[cons](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cons)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _disadvantages, drawbacks_, or a contextually relevant term.

## 󠀁[control](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#control)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

In user documentation, don’t use _control_ when you need to describe the UI element
used to set a value on a continuous range of possible values, such as screen brightness
or volume. Instead, use _slider_.

In other contexts, it’s OK to use _control_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [slider](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#slider).

## 󠀁[copy](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#copy)󠁿

Use instead of _cut_ as a verb to describe temporarily moving text to the clipboard.

You copy a file _to_ a disk, not _on_ a disk or _onto_ a disk.

See also [cut, cut-and-paste](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cut-cut-and-paste),
[move](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#move).

## 󠀁[corrupted](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#corrupted)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, rewrite the sentence to include a more empathetic and inclusive
statement. Offer help in fixing the problem if possible.

Don’t use _corrupt_.

## 󠀁[country, country or region](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#country-country-or-region)󠁿

Avoid using _country_ when referring to a geographical area. Instead, use _country
or region_ or just _region_.

Don’t use _geography_ or _geo_ as a synonym for _country or region_.

It’s OK to use _country/region_ where space is limited.

## 󠀁[cPanel](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cpanel)󠁿

Use lowercase _c_ and capitalize _P_.

## 󠀁[CPU](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cpu)󠁿

Initialism for _central processing unit_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[crash](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#crash)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _fail_ for disks or other hardware, or _stop responding_
for programs or operating systems.

See also [fail](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#fail), 
[stop, stop responding](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop-stop-responding).

## 󠀁[CRUD](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#crud)󠁿

Acronym for _create, read, update, delete_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[CSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#css)󠁿

Initialism for _Cascading Style Sheets_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _CCS
file_ file rather than _.css file_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[CSV](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#csv)󠁿

Initialism for _comma-separated values_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _CSV
file_ file rather than _.csv file_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[Ctrl](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#ctrl)󠁿

Abbreviation for _Control_. Capitalize.

Use _Ctrl_ only in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited. Otherwise, use
_Control_ as in _Control key_ or _Control+C_.

Don’t use _CTRL_ or _ctrl_.

## 󠀁[currently](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#currently)󠁿

Don’t use _currently_ to imply that a feature or functionality might become available
in the future.

**Example**

 **Not recommended:** Full site editor is currently not supported on this theme.

For more information, see [Documenting future features](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/facts-claims/#documenting-future-features).

## 󠀁[cut, cut-and-paste](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cut-cut-and-paste)󠁿

It’s OK to use _cut-and-paste_ as an adjective.

Don’t use _cut-and-paste_ or _cut-and-replace_ as a noun or verb. Instead, use _delete_.
It’s OK to use _paste_ by itself.

Don’t use _cut_ as a verb to describe removing or deleting something. Instead, use
_delete_.

Don’t use _cut_ as a verb to describe temporarily moving text to the clipboard. 
Instead, use _move_ or _copy_.

See also [copy](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#copy),
[delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete), [move](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#move).

## 󠀁[cyber-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/?output_format=md#cyber)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _cyber-_ such as _cybersecurity,
cyberspace,_ and _cyberattack_, unless _cyber-_ is followed by a proper noun or 
it is absolutely necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

---

 * [display](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#display)
 * [display adapter, display driver](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#display-adapter-display-driver)

 * [DNSSEC](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dnssec)
 * [document, documentation](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#document-documentation)
 * [DOM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dom)
 * [domain](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#domain)

 * [double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double-tap-double-tap)

 * [drag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#drag)

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[dash](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dash)󠁿

Don’t use _dash_ to refer to a _hyphen_.

For more information, see [Dashes](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/dashes/)
and [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

## 󠀁[data](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#data)󠁿

Use _data_ as both a singular and plural noun. Don’t use _datum_.

Always use _data_ with a singular verb.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** The data are invalid.

 **Recommended:** The data is invalid.

## 󠀁[dataset](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dataset)󠁿

One word. Not _data set_ or _data-set_.

## 󠀁[data source](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#data-source)󠁿

Two words. Not _datasource_ or _data-source_.

## 󠀁[data type](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#data-type)󠁿

Two words. Not _datatype_ or _data-type_.

## 󠀁[debug](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#debug)󠁿

Use only in the context of software development. Don’t use as a synonym for _troubleshoot_.

## 󠀁[deactivate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#deactivate)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, use _turn off_ or a contextually relevant term.

See also [turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off).

## 󠀁[decrement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#decrement)󠁿

As a verb, use _decrement_ to refer to decreasing an integer count by one. Don’t
use as a synonym for _decrease_.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

## 󠀁[default](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#default)󠁿

It’s OK to use _default_ to describe standard settings or specifications.

## 󠀁[degree](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#degree)󠁿

See [degree symbol](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/symbols/#o-degree-symbol).

## 󠀁[dehighlight](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dehighlight)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, rephrase the sentence or use a contextually relevant term such
as _clear_.

See also [clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#clear).

## 󠀁[deprecate, deprecated](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#deprecate-deprecated)󠁿

Use _deprecate_ or _deprecated_ to describe a product, a service, or a feature that
would be or is unavailable or unsupported.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Instead, use 
_obsolete_ or a contextually relevant term for a general audience.

Don’t use _deprecated_ to mean _removed, deleted, shut down_, or _turned down_.

See also [obsolete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/#obsolete).

## 󠀁[delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#delete)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe removing a file, folder, or other content.

Don’t use _delete_ as a synonym for _remove_. Don’t use _cut_ or erase* as a synonym
for delete.

See also [cut, cut-and-paste](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#cut-cut-and-paste),
[remove](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#remove).

## 󠀁[depress](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#depress)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _press_.

For more information, see [Press](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#press).

See also [press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold).

## 󠀁[deselect](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#deselect)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _clear_ for checkboxes and _cancel the selection_ for other
UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page the user interacts
with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they are doing. elements.

Don’t use _uncheck, unselect, unhighlight_, or _dehighlight_ as a synonym for _deselect_.

See also [clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#clear).

## 󠀁[desire, desired](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#desire-desired)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _want_ or _need_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** If you desire to change the color of the menu, go to **Appearance**.

 **Recommended:** If you want to change the color of the menu, go to **Appearance**.

See also [need](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/#need), 
[want](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/w/#want).

## 󠀁[desktop](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#desktop)󠁿

Don’t use as a noun to refer to a computer. Instead, use _computer, device_, or 
a contextually accurate term.

See also [computer](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#computer),
[device](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#device).

## 󠀁[destination](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#destination)󠁿

Use a more contextually accurate term such as the folder name, instead of _destination_.
Use _destination_ as a modifier only if necessary for clarity.

## 󠀁[device](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#device)󠁿

Use to generically refer to all types of computers, phones, and other hardware devices.

Use a more accurate term such as _mobile phone_ or _computer_ whenever possible.

## 󠀁[dialog](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dialog)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. Refer to a dialog box by its label. If you have to
use a descriptor, use _dialog_ or _dialog box_.

Use _dialog_, not _dialogue_. Use _dialogue_ only for verbal interaction between
people.

For more information, see [Window, page, dialog, and view](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#window-page-dialog-and-view).

## 󠀁[different](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#different)󠁿

Don’t use to mean _various, many,_ or _multiple_.

It’s OK to use difference in comparisons. Use _different than_ only when _than_ 
is followed by a clause.

Don’t use _different to_.

## 󠀁[direction keys, directional keys](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#direction-keys-directional-keys)󠁿

Don’t use _direction keys_ or _directional keys_. Instead, use _arrow keys_.

See also [arrow keys](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/a/#arrow-keys).

## 󠀁[directory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#directory)󠁿

In general, use _folder_ instead of _directory_. It’s OK to use _directory_ for 
consistency, such as when your IDE or command-line uses it.

See also [folder](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#folder).

## 󠀁[dimmed](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dimmed)󠁿

Use to describe a UI element such as a menu item, dropdown list option, or button
that the user can’t interact with due to certain conditions.

In general, describe how the user should interact with the UI rather than describing
the state of the UI. Use _appears dimmed_ for describing its appearance. Also include
how the user can enable it and interact with the element.

See also [disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disable-disabled),
[shaded](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#shaded), [unavailable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#unavailable).

## 󠀁[disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disable-disabled)󠁿

It’s OK to use _disable_ as a verb in developer documentation and for a technical
audience, to mean making a function or feature inactive. Use _disabled_ for such
functions and features. Avoid using in user documentation and for a general audience.

Don’t use _disabled_ to refer to UI elements, functions, or features that are turned
off or unavailable. Instead, use a more accurate term such as _turned off, inactive,_
or _unavailable_.

Don’t use _disabled_ to refer to people with disabilities. For more information,
see [Accessibility and disability](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/inclusivity/#accessibility-and-disability).

See also [enable, enabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#enable-enabled),
[dimmed](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dimmed),
[shaded](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#shaded), [inactive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#inactive),
[turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off),
[unavailable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#unavailable).

## 󠀁[disc](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disc)󠁿

Use _disc_ or _optical disc_ to refer to optical storage media such as CDs or DVDs.

For magnetic storage media such as hard disks, use _disk_.

See also [disk](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disk),
[drive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#drive).

## 󠀁[disk](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disk)󠁿

Use to refer to magnetic storage media such as hard disks.

It’s OK to use _disk_ to generically refer to other types of computer storage such
as flash storage and solid-state drives. For example, terms like _disk image_ and
_disk partition_ are used in the general sense without considering the type of storage.

Instead of _disk_, you can also use a more general term, such as _computer_ or _storage
space_.

For optical storage media such as CDs or DVDs, use _disc_.

See also [disc](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disc),
[drive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#drive).

## 󠀁[display](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#display)󠁿

Don’t use as an intransitive verb. _Display_ is a transitive verb; therefore it 
requires an object.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** The dropdown menu displays.

 **Recommended:** The dropdown menu is displayed.

 **Recommended:** The dropdown menu appears.

Use _display_ as a general term as a noun, to refer to any visual output device 
such as a monitor or a built-in display on most devices. Don’t use _display_ when
you mean _desktop_ or _screen_. Use _screen_ to distinguish the usable portion of
the display from its edges.

See also [appear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/a/#appear).

## 󠀁[display adapter, display driver](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#display-adapter-display-driver)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _video card_ and _video driver_.

See also [video card](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/#video-card),
[video driver](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/#video-driver).

## 󠀁[DMG file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dmg-file)󠁿

Abbreviation for _Disk Image_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _DMG
file_ rather than _.dmg file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

See also [image](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#image),
[IMG file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#img-file).

## 󠀁[DNS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dns)󠁿

Acronym for _Domain Name System_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [DNSSEC](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dnssec).

## 󠀁[DNSSEC](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dnssec)󠁿

Acronym for _Domain Name System Security Extensions_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [DNS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dns).

## 󠀁[document, documentation](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#document-documentation)󠁿

Use _document_ to refer to any editable file such as a _text file_ or a _Word file_.
Use a contextually relevant term such as _presentation_ or _sheet_ whenever possible.

For more information, see [Referring to files](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-files).

Use _in this document_ while referencing in a particular document. Avoid using _in
this article_ or _in this topic_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** This article lists all the available WP-CLIWP-CLI WP-CLI is
the Command Line Interface for WordPress, used to do administrative and development
tasks in a programmatic way. The project page is [http://wp-cli.org/](http://wp-cli.org/)
[https://make.wordpress.org/cli/](https://make.wordpress.org/cli/) commands.

 **Not recommended:** This topic lists all the available WP-CLIWP-CLI WP-CLI is 
the Command Line Interface for WordPress, used to do administrative and development
tasks in a programmatic way. The project page is [http://wp-cli.org/](http://wp-cli.org/)
[https://make.wordpress.org/cli/](https://make.wordpress.org/cli/) commands.

 **Recommended:** This document lists all the available WP-CLIWP-CLI WP-CLI is the
Command Line Interface for WordPress, used to do administrative and development 
tasks in a programmatic way. The project page is [http://wp-cli.org/](http://wp-cli.org/)
[https://make.wordpress.org/cli/](https://make.wordpress.org/cli/) commands.

Use _file_ for general uses such as _file management_ or _file structure_.

See also [file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#file).

## 󠀁[DOM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dom)󠁿

Acronym for _Document Object Model_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[domain](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#domain)󠁿

In general, _domain_ has multiple meanings, such as in internet addresses and databases.
Specify the meaning of _domain_ on the first use.

## 󠀁[double-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double)󠁿

In general, hyphenate compound adjectives beginning with _double-_ such as _double-
layer_ and _double-sided_, unless _double-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is
absolutely necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double-click-double-click)󠁿

Use _double-click_ as a verb to describe selecting most targets such as buttons,
links, list items, and radio buttons by clicking the mouse twice in rapid succession.
Don’t hyphenate as a noun.

For more information, see [Click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#click).

See also [click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#click),
[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double-tap-double-tap),
[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select), [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double-tap-double-tap)󠁿

Use _double-click_ as a verb to describe selecting most targets such as buttons,
links, list items, and radio buttons by clicking the mouse twice in rapid succession.
Don’t hyphenate as a noun.

For more information, see [Tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#tap).

See also [click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#click),
[double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#double-click-double-click),
[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select), [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[downgrade](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#downgrade)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

Use only in the context of downgrading versions, drivers, software, and similar 
subjects.

## 󠀁[download](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#download)󠁿

Use _download_ to refer to user-initiated transfer of data or content to a system
or device. Use _install_ to describe adding programs, apps, other software, and 
hardware to a device.

Ensure that you make it clear whether you’re using _download_ as a noun or verb.

When you use _download_ as a verb, describe what the user is downloading and where
it is being downloaded. It’s OK to use _download_ as a noun.

See also [install](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#install),
[load](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#load), [upload](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#upload).

## 󠀁[drag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#drag)󠁿

Use _drag_, not _drag and drop_ and _click and drag_.

For more information, see [Move, drag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#move-drag).

See also [move](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#move).

## 󠀁[drive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#drive)󠁿

Use to refer to a data storage device such as a hard drive, optical drive, or a 
solid-state drive.

It’s OK to use _drive_ after specifying the type of drive on the first mention.

Don’t use drive when you mean _disk_ or _disc_.

See also [disc](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disc),
[disk](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#disk).

## 󠀁[dropdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dropdown)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. Refer to a dropdown by its label. If you have to use
a descriptor, use _dropdown_.

It’s OK to use _dropdown_ as an adjective. Avoid using _dropdown_ as a noun.

For more information, see [Dropdown list, combo box, and spin box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#dropdown-list-combo-box-and-spin-box).

## 󠀁[dual-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#dual)󠁿

In general, hyphenate compound adjectives beginning with _dual-_ such as _dual-core,
dual-link_ and _dual-band_, unless _dual-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is
absolutely necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[due to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/?output_format=md#due-to)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, use _because of, caused by_, or a contextually relevant alternative.

---

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[e-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#e)󠁿

Shortened abbreviation for _electronic_.

In general, hyphenate words beginning with _e-_ such as _e-learning, e-book_, and
_e-commerce_, unless _e-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely necessary
to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[easy, easily](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#easy-easily)󠁿

Avoid using. What might be easy for one person, may not be easy for others.

## 󠀁[earlier](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#earlier)󠁿

Use _later_ to refer to older versions of a product or software. Don’t use _lower,
older, higher,_, and _newer_ in context of versions.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** To use this function, you must have WordPress 4.2 or lower.

 **Not recommended:** To use this function, you must have WordPress 4.2 or older.

 **Not recommended:** To use this function, you must have WordPress 4.2-.

 **Recommended:** To use this function, you must have WordPress 4.2 or earlier.

See also [later](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#later).

## 󠀁[e-book](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#e-book)󠁿

Hyphenate.

Not _ebook, eBook_ or _e book_.

## 󠀁[e-commerce](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#e-commerce)󠁿

Hyphenate.

Not _ecommerce, eCommerce_ or _e commerce_.

## 󠀁[e.g.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#e-g)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _for example, such as_, or _like_.

See also [like](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#like), 
[such as](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#such-as).

## 󠀁[either, either/or](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#either-either-or)󠁿

Use _either_ only for a choice between two things; avoid using it for a choice between
multiple things.

When writing using _either_, use parallel syntax. It’s OK to write _Do either A 
or B_ or _Either do A or B_, but don’t write _Either do A or B_.

Don’t use _either/or_. Use the complete phrase instead.

## 󠀁[element](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#element)󠁿

In general, use _element_ for HTMLHTML HTML is an acronym for Hyper Text Markup 
Language. It is a markup language that is used in the development of web pages and
websites. and XML items. HTML 4 elements are known as _tags_, but the equivalent
elements in modern HTML and XML are known as _elements_.

## 󠀁[email](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#email)󠁿

One word. Not _e mail_ or _e-mail_.

## 󠀁[embed](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#embed)󠁿

Use instead of _imbed_.

## 󠀁[emoji](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#emoji)󠁿

It’s OK to use emoji to refer to small symbols such as 😃 that represent emoticons,
gestures, concepts, objects, and other symbols in documentation with an informal
tone.

Use lowercase. Use _emoji_ for both singular and plural forms.

Don’t use emoji in documentation or the UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface–
the layout of the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ 
and less about what they are doing. when there’s a serious problem, failure, or 
error.

Use regular punctuation with emoji that appear in running text.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** Look out for new updates 👀!

Ensure that the meaning of your documentation could be conveyed without emoji. Using
emoji may prove to be difficult for accessibilityAccessibility Accessibility (commonly
shortened to a11y) refers to the design of products, devices, services, or environments
for people with disabilities. The concept of accessible design ensures both “direct
access” (i.e. unassisted) and “indirect access” meaning compatibility with a person’s
assistive technology (for example, computer screen readers). (https://en.wikipedia.
org/wiki/Accessibility), localization, or for translation. People with cognitive
impairments, as well as people using assistive technologies such as screen-reading
software and might have difficulty interpreting emoji.

For more information, see [Writing documentation for an international audience](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/global-audience/).

See also [emoticon](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#emoticon).

## 󠀁[emoticon](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#emoticon)󠁿

It’s OK to use emoticons to represent an emotion or a facial expression in documentation
with an informal tone. Generally, emoticons are created with typographic characters
or symbols such as :), :P, or XD.

Don’t use emoticons in documentation or the UI when there’s a serious problem, failure,
or error.

Use regular punctuation with emoji that appear in running text.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** The bug was fixed :).

Ensure that the meaning of your documentation could be conveyed without emoticons.
Using emoticons may prove to be difficult for accessibility, localization, or for
translation. People with cognitive impairments, as well as people using assistive
technologies such as screen-reading software and might have difficulty interpreting
emoticons.

For more information, see [Writing documentation for an international audience](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/global-audience/).

See also [emoji](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#emoji).

## 󠀁[enable, enabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#enable-enabled)󠁿

Use _enable_ to refer to turning on an option or feature or making an action possible.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** To enable full width, select the Site Width toggle button.

Don’t use _enables_ for things that _allow_ you, or _let_ you, or give you the ability
to do something. Instead, rewrite the sentence to emphasize on the task that the
user can accomplish. If you have to express ability to do something, use _lets you_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** The `get` request enables you to retrieve the data.

 **Sometimes okay:** The `get` request lets you retrieve the data.

 **Recommended:** You can retrieve the data using the `get` request.

Don’t use _enabled_ to mean _selected_ such as while referring to radio buttons 
or checkboxes.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Ensure that your choice is enabled.

 **Recommended:** Ensure that your choice is selected.

For more information, see [Switch, turn on, turn off, enable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#switch-turn-on-turn-off-enable).

See also [disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#disable-disabled),
[turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off).

## 󠀁[end](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#end)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe stopping an ongoing process. Use _close_ for applications
and programs.

See also [close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#close),
[exit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#exit), [interrupt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#interrupt),
[stop](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop).

## 󠀁[endpoint](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#endpoint)󠁿

One word. Not _end point_ or _end-point_.

## 󠀁[end user, end-user](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#end-user-end-user)󠁿

Two words as a noun. Hyphenate as an adjective.

See also [user](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#user).

## 󠀁[enter](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#enter)󠁿

Use when referring to the action of the user entering text, or inserting a value.

For more information, see [Enter, type](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#enter-type).

See also [type](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#type).

## 󠀁[entry field](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#entry-field)󠁿

It’s OK to use _entry field_ in a database context, in developer documentation, 
and for a technical audience.

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

Don’t refer to a text box or text field as an _entry field_. Refer to a text box
by its label. If you have to use a descriptor, use _text box_.

For more information, see [Text box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#text-box).

## 󠀁[erase](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#erase)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _delete_.

See also [delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete).

## 󠀁[et al.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#et-al)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _and others_.

It’s OK to use _et al._ in a citation that includes three or more authors.

## 󠀁[etc.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#etc)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _such as_ or _like_ followed by some examples.

Don’t use _and so on_.

See also [like](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#like), 
[such as](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#such-as).

## 󠀁[exe file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#exe-file)󠁿

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _executable
file_ rather than _.exe file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[execute](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#execute)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

Avoid using in user documentation and for a general audience. Instead, use _run_.

## 󠀁[exit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#exit)󠁿

Don’t use to describe closing a program or an application.

For more information see [Close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#close).

See also [close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#close),
[end](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#end), [interrupt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#interrupt),
[stop](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop).

## 󠀁[expand](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#expand)󠁿

Use to describe an action which displays more items or relevant elements in the 
UI.

## 󠀁[exploit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#exploit)󠁿

Don’t use to mean _use_. Only use _exploit_ in the negative sense.

## 󠀁[extract](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/?output_format=md#extract)󠁿

Use instead of _unarchive_ or _uncompress_.

For more information, see [File interactions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#file-interactions).

---

## 󠀁[fail](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#fail)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _stop responding_ or
a contextually relevant term in user documentation.

See also [stop, stop responding](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop-stop-responding).

## 󠀁[fail over, failover](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#fail-over-failover)󠁿

Two words as a verb, one word as a noun or an adjective. Avoid using in user documentation
and for a general audience.

## 󠀁[FAQ](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#faq)󠁿

Initialism for _Frequently Asked Questions_. Use uppercase.

Use _an FAQ_, not _a FAQ_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[far-left, far-right](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#far-left-far-right)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _leftmost_ or _rightmost_.

In general, avoid using directional language such as _left, right, up, down_ in 
instructions to locate UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of 
the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about
what they are doing. elements or other content. Directional language proves to be
difficult for accessibilityAccessibility Accessibility (commonly shortened to a11y)
refers to the design of products, devices, services, or environments for people 
with disabilities. The concept of accessible design ensures both “direct access”(
i.e. unassisted) and “indirect access” meaning compatibility with a person’s assistive
technology (for example, computer screen readers). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/
Accessibility) or for localization. People with cognitive impairments, as well as
people using assistive technologies such as screen-reading software and might have
difficulty interpreting directional language. If a particular UI element or other
content is difficult to convey, include a screenshot or illustration.

For more information, see [Procedures and instructions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/procedures/).

## 󠀁[field](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#field)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

Don’t use to refer to a text-entry box. Instead, refer to the box by its label. 
If you have to use a descriptor, use _box_ instead of _field_.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

## 󠀁[file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#file)󠁿

Whenever possible, use a more specific term, such as _document, zip file_, or _CSSCSS
CSS is an acronym for cascading style sheets. This is what controls the design or
look and feel of a site. file_.

See also [filename](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#filename).

## 󠀁[filename](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#filename)󠁿

One word. Not _file name_ or _file-name_.

For more information, see [Filenames](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/).

## 󠀁[filesystem](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#filesystem)󠁿

One word. Not _file system_ or _file-system_.

## 󠀁[fill in, fill out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#fill-in-fill-out)󠁿

Use _fill in_ when referring to entering information in individual fields. Use _fill
out_ when referring to completing an entire form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** Fill out the contact form. Be sure to fill in the required fields.

## 󠀁[finalize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#finalize)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _finish_ or _complete_.

## 󠀁[find and replace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#find-and-replace)󠁿

Use _find_ and _replace_ as separate verbs, not a single verb phrase such as _find
and replace_.

Don’t use _find and replace_ or _find-and-replace_ as a noun or an adjective.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Do a find and replace of the user ID.

 **Recommended:** Find the user ID and replace it with the username.

Don’t use _global_ to describe finding and replacing. Instead, use _all instances_
or _all occurrences_.

Use _find characters_ and _replacement characters_ to describe what the customer
enters into a find or replace box.

## 󠀁[firmware](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#firmware)󠁿

One word. Not _firm ware_ or _firm-ware_.

## 󠀁[flag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#flag)󠁿

Don’t use in a command-line context. Instead, use _option_.

For more information, see [Command-line syntax](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/).

## 󠀁[flick](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#flick)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _swipe_.

See also [swipe](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#swipe).

## 󠀁[flush, flush to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#flush-flush-to)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience. Don’t use _flush, flush to, flush
left_, or _flush right_ to describe text alignment. Instead, use _even, left-aligned_,
or _right-aligned_, as appropriate.

See also [left align, left-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#left-align-left-aligned),
[right align, right-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#right-align-right-aligned).

## 󠀁[folder](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#folder)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. In developer content, folders are usually referred
to as _directories_.

Not all folders contain files or other folders. Describe the nature or appearance
of the folder if necessary.

In procedures and instructions, use bold formatting for the folder name if you’re
instructing the user to interact with the folder.

For more instructions, see [Procedures and instructions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/procedures/)
and [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[following](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#following)󠁿

Use _following_ as an adjective to introduce a table, list, or other content. If
_following_ is the last word before what it introduces, follow it with a colon.

**Examples**

 **Recommended:** The following table shows the BlockBlock Block is the abstract
term used to describe units of markup that, composed together, form the content 
or layout of a webpage using the WordPress editor. The idea combines concepts of
what in the past may have achieved with shortcodes, custom HTML, and embed discovery
into a single consistent API and user experience. APIAPI An API or Application Programming
Interface is a software intermediary that allows programs to interact with each 
other and share data in limited, clearly defined ways. reference:

 **Recommended:** Do the following:

For more information, see [Table placement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/tables/#table-placement)
and [Lists](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/lists/).

## 󠀁[font, font style, font size](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#font-font-style-font-size)󠁿

Use _font_, not _font family, typeface_, or _face_ for the name of a typeface design
such as _Helvetica_.

To refer to the formatting, such as bold, underlined, or italic, use _font style_,
not _type style_ or _typeface attribute_.

Use _font size_, not _type size_ for the point size such as 10 points or 12 points.

For information about when to use various font styles, see [Text formatting](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/text/).

## 󠀁[foo, foobar, fubar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#foo-foobar-fubar)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, use a clearer and more meaningful placeholder with relevant
text.

For more information, see [Placeholders](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/placeholders/).

## 󠀁[footer](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#footer)󠁿

Use instead of _bottom running head_ or _running foot_.

See also [header](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/h/#header).

## 󠀁[foreign](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#foreign)󠁿

Don’t use to describe any geographic locations. Instead, use the names of the respective
countries or regions, or use phrases such as _countries other than the US_ and _US
only_.

## 󠀁[for instance](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#for-instance)󠁿

Avoid when possible. Instead, use _for example_ or _such as_.

## 󠀁[format, formatted, formatting](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#format-formatted-formatting)󠁿

Use _format_ to refer to the overall layout, arrangement, or appearance of text,
graphics and other elements in a document.

Use _formatting_ or _formatted_ to refer to specific character formatting, paragraph
formatting, and other types of formatting.

For more information, see [Document structure](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/document-structure/)
and [Text formatting](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/text/).

See also [font, font style](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#font-font-style).

## 󠀁[freeze, frozen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#freeze-frozen)󠁿

Don’t use _freeze_ as a synonym for _stop responding_. Don’t use frozen to describe
the resulting state.

Instead, use _stop_ or _stop responding_ when a program encounters a problem and
can’t close itself.

See also [stop, stop responding](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop-stop-responding).

## 󠀁[from](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#from)󠁿

Use to indicate a specific place or time as a starting point.

**Examples**

 **Recommended:** The `$wpdb` object can be used to read data from any table in 
the WordPress database.

 **Recommended:** You can import content into your site from another WordPress site
using the WordPress Import tool.

## 󠀁[front end, front-end](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#front-end-front-end)󠁿

Two words as a noun, hyphenate as an adjective.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _interface, program,
app_, or a contextually relevant and accurate term.

## 󠀁[FTP](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#ftp)󠁿

Initialism for _File Transfer Protocol_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[full-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#full)󠁿

Use a hyphen in compound adjectives beginning with _full-_.

**Examples**

 * full-size
 * full-page
 * full-time

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[full screen, full-screen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#full-screen-full-screen)󠁿

Two words as a noun. Hyphenate as an adjective before a noun.

## 󠀁[functionality](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/?output_format=md#functionality)󠁿

Avoid using. Use only to refer to a set of functions and their specified properties.

Whenever possible, use a simpler term such as _features_ instead.
