## 󠀁[machine](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#machine)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for computer.

## 󠀁[macOS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#macos)󠁿

Operating system used on Apple Macintosh computers. Use lowercase for _mac_ and 
uppercase for _OS_.

See also [OS, operating system](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/#os-operating-system).

## 󠀁[manipulate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#manipulate)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _work with, handle_, or _use_.

## 󠀁[MariaDB](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mariadb)󠁿

Capitalize _M_ and use uppercase for _DB_.

## 󠀁[Markdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#markdown)󠁿

Capitalize.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _Markdown
file_ rather than _.md file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[marquee](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#marquee)󠁿

OK to use when referring to the scrolling text feature or tag.

## 󠀁[markup, mark up](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#markup-mark-up)󠁿

One word as a noun. As a verb, use two words as in _mark up_. Don’t hyphenate in
any form.

## 󠀁[master, master/slave](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#master-master-slave)󠁿

Avoid using whenever possible. Instead, replace _master_ with a contextually relevant
term such as _primary, main, original, parent, initiator, driver, controller, manager,
mixer, aggregator, publisher, leader_, or _active_. Use _primary/secondary, primary/
subordinate, principal/agent_ or other relevant terms instead of _master/slave_.

For more information, see [Replacing established terms](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/inclusivity/#replacing-established-terms).

## 󠀁[mathematical](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mathematical)󠁿

Use instead of _mathematic_.

## 󠀁[matrix, matrices](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#matrix-matrices)󠁿

Use the plural _matrixes_ unless there is a domain-specific reason (for example,
a mathematical context) to use _matrices_.

## 󠀁[may](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#may)󠁿

Avoid using in standard documentation; reserve _may_ for official policy or legal
considerations. To convey possibility, use _might_ instead. To convey permission,
use _can_ instead.

See also [can](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#can)

## 󠀁[maximize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#maximize)󠁿

Use to refer to making a window as big as possible without going full screen.

See also [minimize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#minimize).

## 󠀁[MB, megabyte](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mb-megabyte)󠁿

Initialism for _megabyte_. Use uppercase.

One _MB_ equals 1000^(2) bytes in the context of file size or storage capacity, 
and 1024^(2) bytes in the context of computer memory.

In the noun form, insert a space between the numeral and the abbreviation. Use the
preposition _of_ before the unit.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 128 MB of storage

Don’t hyphenate the adjective form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** a 16 MB storage drive

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[Mbit, megabit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mbit-megabit)󠁿

Initialism for _megabit_.

One _Mbit_ equals 1000^(2) bits in the context of file size or storage capacity,
and 1024^(2) bits in the context of computer memory.

In the noun form, insert a space between the numeral and the abbreviation. Use the
preposition _of_ before the unit.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 10 MBit of memory

Don’t hyphenate the adjective form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 10 MBit memory

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[Mbps (Mbit/s), megabits per second](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mbps-mbit-s-megabits-per-second)󠁿

Initialism for _megabits per second_.

For more information, see [Units of measurement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/units-of-measurement/).

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [Mbit, megabit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mbit-megabit).

## 󠀁[MBps (MB/s), megabytes per second](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mbps-mb-s-megabytes-per-second)󠁿

Initialism for _megabytes per second_.

For more information, see [Units of measurement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/units-of-measurement/).

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [MB, megabyte](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mb-megabyte).

## 󠀁[media, medium](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#media-medium)󠁿

Use _medium_ as a singular subject and _media_ as a plural subject. Accordingly,
use the correct verb form; _the medium is_ and _the media are_.

However, when discussing audio, video, and images, you can use _media_ as a singular
subject to describe a collection of content such as a set of images.

## 󠀁[mega-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mega)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _mega-_ such as _megabit, megabyte,
megahertz,_ and _megapixel_, unless _mega-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is
absolutely necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[memory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#memory)󠁿

In most cases, refer to a specific kind of memory, such as _random-access memory(
RAM), read-only memory (ROM), virtual memory_, or _portable storage devices_.

In the noun forms that refer to memory measurements, use _of_ in a prepositional
phrase before the unit, such as _512 MB of RAM_.

Don’t use memory to refer to storage capacity; instead, use a term such as _storage
space_.

See also [storage](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#storage).

## 󠀁[menu bar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#menu-bar)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page
the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they
are doing. element.

For more information, see [Menu bar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#menu-bar).

## 󠀁[menu item](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#menu-item)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements).

## 󠀁[message](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#message)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use _send, receive,_ or a contextually relevant term.

OK to use as a noun. If required, you can also provide adjective to present further
context, such as _text message, email message, audio message_ or _video message_.

## 󠀁[meta](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#meta)󠁿

For the [Make WordPress Meta Team](https://make.wordpress.org/meta/), capitalize
_MetaMeta Meta is a term that refers to the inside workings of a group. For us, 
this is the team that works on internal WordPress sites like WordCamp Central and
Make WordPress._.

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _meta-_ such as _metadata,_ and
_metafeed_, unless _meta-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely necessary
to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

## 󠀁[metadata](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#metadata)󠁿

One word. Not _meta data_ or _meta-data_.

## 󠀁[method](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#method)󠁿

In the context developer documentation or for a technical audience, where _method_
refers to a member of a class, avoid also using _method_ as a synonym for _manner_
or _approach_.

## 󠀁[MHz, megahertz](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mhz-megahertz)󠁿

Initialism for _megahertz_.

In the noun form, insert a space between the numeral and the abbreviation. Use the
preposition _of_ before the unit.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** a rate of 5.0 MHz

Don’t hyphenate the adjective form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** a 5.0 MHz rate

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[micro-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#micro)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _micro-_ such as _microprocessor,
microservices,_ and _microcomputer_ unless _micro-_ is followed by a proper noun
or it is absolutely necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[Microsoft](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#microsoft)󠁿

OK to use. Capitalize.

See also [Windows](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/w/#windows).

## 󠀁[midnight](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#midnight)󠁿

OK to use, but not when paired with time in the numeral format.

**Example**

 **Not recommended:** _12:00 midnight_

For more information, see [Dates and times](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/dates-times/).

## 󠀁[migrate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#migrate)󠁿

Use to move databases, media, users, applications or code, from one server, environment
or platform to another. Don’t use as a synonym for _upgrade_ or _port_.

## 󠀁[million, M](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#million-m)󠁿

Don’t abbreviate _million_ as _M, m_, or _mn_. Spell out the word or denote the 
entire number.

For more information, see [Abbreviations in numbers](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/numbers/#abbreviations).

## 󠀁[MIME](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mime)󠁿

Abbreviation for _Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[minimize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#minimize)󠁿

Use to refer to placing the window in the taskbar or dock.

See also [maximize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#maximize).

## 󠀁[ML](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#ml)󠁿

Abbreviation for _machine learning_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[mobile, mobile device, mobile phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mobile-mobile-device-mobile-phone)󠁿

Use instead of _cell phone_.

See also [phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#phone).

## 󠀁[mobile data](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mobile-data)󠁿

Use instead of _cellular data_.

## 󠀁[mobile network](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mobile-network)󠁿

Use instead of _cellular network_.

## 󠀁[monospace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#monospace)󠁿

One word. Not _mono space_ or _mono-space_.

## 󠀁[more than](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#more-than)󠁿

Use to describe items or elements that are quantifiable such as amounts or figures.

Don’t use _over_.

See also [later](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#later),
[over](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/#over).

## 󠀁[mount](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mount)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe the action of making a disk or disk image available.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience.

See also [unmount](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#unmount).

## 󠀁[mouse](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mouse)󠁿

Avoid referring to the mouse whenever possible. Instead, emphasize on the task to
be accomplished, and the interaction verb with the mouse such as _select, click,_
or _press_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

## 󠀁[mouse over](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mouse-over)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _move the mouse pointer to_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

## 󠀁[movable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#movable)󠁿

Not _moveable_.

## 󠀁[move](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#move)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe transferring files, folders, or UI elements from one location
to another.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#move-drag).

See also [drag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#drag), 
[copy](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#copy).

## 󠀁[MP3](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mp3)󠁿

Initialism for _MPEG Audio Layer 3_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _MP3
file_ rather than _.mp3 file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[MP4](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mp4)󠁿

Initialism for _MPEG-4_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _MP4
file_ rather than _.mp4 file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

See also [MPEG](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mpeg).

## 󠀁[MPEG](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mpeg)󠁿

Acronym for _Moving Picture Experts Group_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _MPEG
file_ rather than _.mpg file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[multi-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#multi)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _multi-_ such as _multimedia, multilevel,
multisiteMultisite Multisite is a WordPress feature which allows users to create
a network of sites on a single WordPress installation. Available since WordPress
version 3.0, Multisite is a continuation of WPMU or WordPress Multiuser project.
WordPress MultiUser project was discontinued and its features were included into
WordPress core. [Advanced Administration Handbook -> Create A Network.](https://developer.wordpress.org/advanced-administration/multisite/create-network/),_
and _multiuser_, unless _multi-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely
necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[multisite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#multisite)󠁿

One word. Not _multi site_ or _multi-site_.

## 󠀁[multitask, multitasking](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#multitask-multitasking)󠁿

Don’t use _multitask_ as a verb. OK to use _multitasking_ as a noun or an adjective.

## 󠀁[must](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#must)󠁿

Use to refer to a task that a user is required to do. Don’t use _must_ to indicate
suggestions or a condescending tone.

For example, _You should set a strong password_ is a suggestion, whereas _You must
set a strong password_ is a requirement.

For more information, see [Style, voice, and tone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/style-voice-tone/).

See also [should](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#should).

## 󠀁[MySQL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/?output_format=md#mysql)󠁿

Capitalize _M_ and use uppercase for _SQL_.

---

## N

# N

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[n](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#n)󠁿

Use lowercase and use italic formatting when using as a variable or placeholder.

For more information, see [Placeholders](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/placeholders/).

## 󠀁[N/A](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#n-a)󠁿

Abbreviation for _not available_ or _not applicable_. Spell out on first reference.

Not _NA, N-A,_ or _na_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[name server](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#name-server)󠁿

Two words. Not _nameserver_ or _name-server_.

## 󠀁[namespace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#namespace)󠁿

One word. Not _name space_ or _name-space_.

## 󠀁[native](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#native)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, use a more accurate term such as _coreCore Core is the set
of software required to run WordPress. The Core Development Team builds WordPress._
or _built-in_ whenever possible.

For more information, see [Replacing established terms](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/inclusivity/#replacing-established-terms).

## 󠀁[navigate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#navigate)󠁿

Avoid using to describe going from one place to other on the internet or other networks.
Instead, use _browse_.

To describe going directly to a website or webpage, whether by entering a URLURL
A specific web address of a website or web page on the Internet, such as a website’s
URL www.wordpress.org or selecting a link, use _go to_.

Avoid using _navigate_ for interacting with UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface–
the layout of the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ 
and less about what they are doing. elements.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

See also [go to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/g/#go-to).

## 󠀁[need](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#need)󠁿

Use _need_ to refer to a requirement or obligation. Don’t use _desire_ or _wish_
as a synonym for _need_.

Use _want_ when the user has a choice of actions or when they are optional.

See also [want](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/w/#want).

## 󠀁[neither](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#neither)󠁿

Write _neither A nor B_, not _neither A or B_.

## 󠀁[network](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#network)󠁿

Don’t abbreviate to _net_. Don’t use _network_ as a verb to refer to the action 
of connecting a computer to a network.

Computers are _on_, not _in_, a network; and computers on a network are _linked_
or _connected_, not _networked_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[new](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#new)󠁿

In most cases, avoid describing a product or feature as _new_ as it is likely to
become out of date. Instead, state the version of software in which the feature 
or product was introduced.

## 󠀁[newer](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#newer)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _later_ to refer to subsequent versions of a product 
or software. Instead, use _later_.

See also [earlier](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#earlier),
[later](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#later).

## 󠀁[NGINX](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#nginx)󠁿

Acronym for _engine X_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[non-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#non)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _non-_ such as _nonstandard, noncompliant,_
and _nonrestrictive_, unless _non-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely
necessary to avoid confusion.

Don’t use _non-_ to negate an entire phrase.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** non-numbered steps or instructions

 **Recommended:** steps or instructions that are not numbered

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[nonprintable, nonprinting](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#nonprintable-nonprinting)󠁿

Use _nonprintable_ to refer to an area of a page that can’t be printed on. Use _nonprinting_
to refer to characters and other data that can’t or won’t be printed.

Don’t use _unprintable_.

## 󠀁[normal, normally](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#normal-normally)󠁿

Don’t use _normal_ to as a synonym for _usual, typical, common_, or a similar term.
Don’t use _normally_ as a synonym for _usually, typically, commonly, often, generally,_
or a similar term.

## 󠀁[notification](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#notification)󠁿

Use instead of _notice_ to describe information displayed to a user such as errors,
updates, or other communications. Don’t use _pop-up, toast_, or _banner_.

For more information about notice types in WordPress, see [Notices](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/notices/).

## 󠀁[number](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#number)󠁿

OK to abbreviate as _no._ in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited. It’s
acceptable to abbreviate _number_ as _no._, but consider a global audience; as many
languages don’t abbreviate _number_ as _no._ which may cause confusion.

For more information about formatting numbers, see [Numbers](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/numbers/).

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [# (number sign)](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/symbols/#number-sign).

## 󠀁[null](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#null)󠁿

Use lowercase _null_ to refer to a null value. Whenever possible, use _null value_
to avoid confusion with the constant.

Use uppercase _NULL_ or capitalized _Null_ only to refer to the constant.

## 󠀁[numeric](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/n/?output_format=md#numeric)󠁿

Use instead of _numerical_.

For the keypad, use _numeric keypad_. Don’t use _numerical keypad_ or _numeric keyboard_.

---

## 󠀁[O2](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#o2)󠁿

Capitalize.

Not _o2, O-2,_ or _O 2_.

See also [P2](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#p2).

## 󠀁[object](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#object)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _thing_ or _item_. Instead, refer to a specific object
or use a contextually relevant and accurate term.

## 󠀁[obsolete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#obsolete)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use a phrase such as _make obsolete_.

## 󠀁[of](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#of)󠁿

Don’t use after another preposition in phrases such as _off of_ or _outside of_.

## 󠀁[offline](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offline)󠁿

One word, both as an adjective and adverb. Not _off line_ or _off-line_.

Use only to describe not being connected to the internet or a particular network.

## 󠀁[off-premises, on-premises](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#off-premises-on-premises)󠁿

Not _off-premise_ and _on-premise_. Hyphenate.

See also [offsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offsite),
[onsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onsite).

## 󠀁[offscreen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offscreen)󠁿

One word. Not _off screen_ or _off-screen_.

See also [onscreen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onscreen).

## 󠀁[offsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offsite)󠁿

One word. Not _off site_ or _off-site_.

See also [off-premises, on-premises](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#off-premises-on-premises),
[onsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onsite).

## 󠀁[OK](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#ok)󠁿

Not _ok, okay, Okay, alright_, or _all right_. Use uppercase.

## 󠀁[older](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#older)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _earlier_ to refer to older versions of a product or 
software. Instead, use _earlier_.

See also [earlier](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#earlier),
[later](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#later).

## 󠀁[once](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#once)󠁿

Use only to describe _one time_. Don’t use as a synonym for _after_ or _when_.

## 󠀁[online](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#online)󠁿

One word, both as an adjective and adverb. Not _on line_ or _on-line_.

Use to describe content or services that are available on the internet or a particular
network. It is OK to use _online_ to describe being on or connected to the internet
or a particular network; but in most cases, use a contextually relevant and accurate
term such as _signed in_ or _connected to the internet_.

See also [offline](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offline).

## 󠀁[onscreen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onscreen)󠁿

One word. Not _on screen_ or _on-screen_.

See also [offscreen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offscreen).

## 󠀁[onsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onsite)󠁿

One word. Not _on site_ or _on-site_.

See also [off-premises, on-premises](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#off-premises-on-premises),
[offsite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#offsite).

## 󠀁[onto, on to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#onto-on-to)󠁿

Use _onto_ to refer to moving something to a position on top of something else.

Use _on to_ when _on_ is part of the verb.

**Examples**

 **Recommended:** Drag the image onto the desktop.

 **Recommended:** Pass on to the next item.

See also [into, in to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#into-in-to).

## 󠀁[open](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#open)󠁿

Use _open_, not _start_ or _launch_ to describe opening a program, application, 
folder, or a similar target. Don’t use _open_ for menus and commands.

Use _open_, not _opened_, to describe the open state, such as _an open folder_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs]https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-
guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#open).

See also [close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#close).

## 󠀁[open source](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#open-source)󠁿

Two words, both as an adjective and verb. Not _opensource_ or _open-source_. Use
lowercase and don’t hyphenate.

## 󠀁[option](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#option)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

In a command-line context, use _option_ instead of _flag, argument_, or _parameter_.

For more information, see [Command-line syntax](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/).

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page
the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they
are doing. element. Refer to an option by its label. If you have to use a descriptor,
use _option_ or _option button_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[OS, operating system](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#os-operating-system)󠁿

Initialism for _operating system_. Use uppercase for the initialism.

For the spelled out version, use two words as a noun, and hyphenate as an adjective.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[output](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#output)󠁿

Avoid as a verb. Instead, use _write to, display on, print on, print to_, or a contextually
relevant and accurate term.

## 󠀁[outside](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#outside)󠁿

Not _outside of_.

## 󠀁[over](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#over)󠁿

Use to refer to a location or position above something.

In context of quantities, don’t use as a synonym for _more than_.

Don’t use to refer to version numbers. Instead, use _later_.

See also [later](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#later),
[more than](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#more-than)

## 󠀁[⁠override](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#%e2%81%a0override)󠁿

One word. Not _over ride_ or _over-ride_.

## 󠀁[overwrite](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/?output_format=md#overwrite)󠁿

Use only to describe existing data with new data. Use _replace_ to describe replacing
an existing file with a new one that has the same name.

Don’t use as a synonym for _type over_.

---

## 󠀁[P2](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#p2)󠁿

Capitalize.

Not _p2, P-2,_ or _P 2_.

See also [O2](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/o/#o2).

## 󠀁[page](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#page-2)󠁿

Use _page_ or _webpage_ to describe a sub-page, document, or a collection of documents
that make up a website or document.

Use _page_ to refer to the page the reader or user is on, such as the home page.

## 󠀁[pane](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pane)󠁿

Use to refer to a smaller section or area that is part of the application window.
Generally, a _pane_ or _view_ is adjacent to other UIUI UI is an acronym for User
Interface – the layout of the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they 
doing that’ and less about what they are doing. elements and regions, and cannot
be hidden, whereas a window is separate and can be hidden.

For more information, see [Window, page, dialog, and view](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#window-page-dialog-and-view).

## 󠀁[parameter](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#parameter)󠁿

Use for a value given to a variable until an operation is completed. Don’t use to
mean _characteristic, element, limit_, or _boundary_.

## 󠀁[parent/child](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#parent-child)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _clear, delete_, or 
_remove_.

Not _parent – child_ or _parent—child_. Don’t use as a synonym for a primary/subordinate
relationship.

## 󠀁[parenthesis, parentheses](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#parenthesis-parentheses)󠁿

Use _opening parenthesis_ or _closing parenthesis_ for an individual parenthesis.
Don’t use _open parenthesis, close parenthesis, beginning parenthesis, ending parenthesis,
left parenthesis_, or _right parenthesis_. It’s OK to use parenthesis by itself 
if it doesn’t matter or it’s clear which parenthesis is being discussed.

For more information, see [Parentheses](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/parentheses/).

## 󠀁[path](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#path)󠁿

OK to use. Avoid using _pathname_ or _path name_ if possible.

Use _address_ or _URLURL A specific web address of a website or web page on the 
Internet, such as a website’s URL www.wordpress.org_, not _path_, to refer to a 
location on the internet.

In general, use _path of_, not _path to_, to refer to the location of a file.

For more information about slashes in paths, see [Slashes with file paths and names](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/slashes/#slashes-with-file-paths-and-names).

For more information about paths in command-line syntax, see [Command prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/command-line-syntax/#command-prompt).

## 󠀁[PC](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pc)󠁿

Initialism for _personal computer_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use _PC_ in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited.

See also [computer](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#computer).

## 󠀁[PDF](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pdf)󠁿

Initialism for _Portable Document Format_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _PDF
file_ file rather than _.pdf file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[per](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#per)󠁿

Use _per_ instead of the division slash (/) to express a rate, unless space constraints
in UI, tables, or headings require the use of the slash.

Avoid using _per_ in contexts other than rate units.

Don’t use _per_ to mean _by_ or _in accordance with_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** transactions/hour

 **Recommended:** transactions per hour

 **Not recommended:** per the style guide

 **Recommended:** according to the style guide

 **Not recommended:** Replace the variable per instance.

 **Recommended:** Replace the variable for each instance.

For more information, see [Units of measurement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/units-of-measurement/#rates).

## 󠀁[percent, percentage](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#percent-percentage)󠁿

Always precede _percent_ with a numeral, no matter how small the value.

It’s OK to use the percent sign (%) in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited.
You can also use the percent sign as a technical symbol.

Use _percentage_ when you describe a nonspecific quantity, or when applying the 
percentage formula.

## 󠀁[Perl](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#perl)󠁿

Acronym for _Practical Extraction and Report Language_. Capitalize.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _Perl
file_ rather than _.pl file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[permalink](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#permalink)󠁿

One word. Not _perma link_ or _perma-link_.

## 󠀁[personally identifiable information](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#personally-identifiable-information)󠁿

OK to use. It’s acceptable to abbreviate _personally identifiable information_ as
_PII_ after the first mention of the term.

## 󠀁[phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#phone)󠁿

It’s OK to use _phone, mobile, mobile device,_ and _mobile phone_.

Don’t use _cell phone_.

## 󠀁[photo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#photo)󠁿

OK to use as an abbreviation for _photograph_. You can also refer to photos as _images_
or _pictures_.

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use _photograph_ or _take a picture_.

## 󠀁[PHP](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#php)󠁿

Initialism for _Hypertext Preprocessor_ (earlier called _Personal Home Page_). Use
uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _PHPPHP
PHP (recursive acronym for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open source
general-purpose scripting language that is especially suited for web development
and can be embedded into HTML. [https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php](https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php)
file_ file rather than _.php file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[phpMyAdmin](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#phpmyadmin)󠁿

Note capitalization.

## 󠀁[picture](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#picture)󠁿

OK to use as a synonym for _photo_ and in standard phrases such as _profile picture_.

See also [photo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#photo).

## 󠀁[placeholder](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#placeholder)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb.

For more information, see [Placeholders](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/placeholders/).

## 󠀁[plaintext, plain text](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#plaintext-plain-text)󠁿

In cryptography contexts, use _plaintext_. Otherwise, use _plain text_.

## 󠀁[please](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#please)󠁿

Don’t use _please_ in standard contexts such as procedures, instructions, or tutorials.

Use _please_ only when the user is asked to do something inconvenient, the application
or site is to blame for the situation, or when there is an issue with the product.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** If the issue persists, please contact your administrator.

For more information, see [Style, voice, and tone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/style-voice-tone/).

## 󠀁[plugin, plug-in, plug in](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#plugin-plug-in-plug-in)󠁿

One word as a noun. As a verb, use two words as in _plug in_. Hyphenate as an adjective
as in _plug-in_.

## 󠀁[PM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pm)󠁿

See [AM, PM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/a/#am-pm).

## 󠀁[PNG](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#png)󠁿

Initialism for _Portable Network Graphics_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _PNG
file_ file rather than _.png file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[point to](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#point-to)󠁿

It’s OK to use _point to_ as a verb to describe moving the mouse pointer over an
area of the UI without selecting it.

Don’t use _point, mouse over_ or _hover the pointer over_.

For more information, see [Hold, hold the pointer over](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#hold-hold-the-pointer-over).

## 󠀁[populate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#populate)󠁿

Avoid using to describe filling out forms. Use with caution to describe populating
a table or other entity.

Don’t use in the context of describing people; instead, use _fill in_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** After populating the form, submit it.

 **Recommended:** After filling out the form, submit it.

 **Recommended:** The SQL command populates the table with sample data.

## 󠀁[pop-up](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pop-up)󠁿

Don’t use as a noun.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** A pop-up

 **Recommended:** A pop-up window

Don’t use pop up or pops up as a verb to describe the appearance of a window. Instead,
use _open_ or a similar verb.

For more information, see [UI elements and interaction](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[port](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#port)󠁿

OK to use the verb forms _port_ and _port to_ in developer documentation and for
a technical audience in the context of portability. Avoid using in user documentation
and for a general audience.

Use _port_ as a noun to refer to a location for passing data in and out of a computer
or device. Don’t use _connector_ to refer to a port.

For the noun form of _port_ in the context of computer networking, use _listen on_,
not _listen to_.

## 󠀁[possible](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#possible)󠁿

Don’t use _possible_ or _impossible_ to mean _you can_ or _you can’t_.

## 󠀁[post-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#post)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _post-_ such as _postdate_ and 
_postgraduate_, unless _post-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely 
necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[pound key, pound sign](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pound-key-pound-sign)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _number sign_.

See also [# (number sign)](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/symbols/#number-sign).

## 󠀁[power down, power up, power off, power on](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#power-down-power-up-power-off-power-on)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _turn off_ and _turn on_.

Don’t use _shut down_ to refer to turning off a device.

See also [turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off),
[shut down, shutdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#shut-down-shutdown),
[start, restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#start-restart).

## 󠀁[pre-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pre)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _pre-_ such as _preexisting_ and
_preinstalled_, unless _pre-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely necessary
to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[preceding](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#preceding)󠁿

It’s OK to use _preceding, previous_, or _earlier_, but link to the particular information
or use a cross-reference when possible.

For more information, see the [Linking](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/linking/)
section.

## 󠀁[predefined](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#predefined)󠁿

One word. Not _pre defined_ or _pre-defined_.

## 󠀁[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#press-press-and-hold)󠁿

Use only to describe pushing a physical button on a device or hardware.

For more information see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#press).

See also [click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#click),
[double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-click-double-click),
[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-tap-double-tap),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select), [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[primitive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#primitive)󠁿

Use with caution. Don’t use _primitive_ in a disparaging sense.

## 󠀁[privileges](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#privileges)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _permissions_ or _rights_.

## 󠀁[program](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#program)󠁿

See [app, application](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/a/#app-application).

## 󠀁[prompt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#prompt)󠁿

Use only to describe a signal, which might or might not be a message, that an app
or the operating system is waiting for the user to take some action. In general,
restrict the use of _prompt_ as a noun to the command prompt.

Use as a verb to refer to the act of requesting information or an action from the
user.

## 󠀁[pros](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pros)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _advantages_ or a contextually relevant term.

## 󠀁[pull down, pull-down](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#pull-down-pull-down)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

Don’t use _pull down_ as a verb to describe how to use a menu or list. Don’t use
_pull-down_ as an adjective to describe the appearance of a menu or list.

For more information, see [Dropdown list, combo box, and spin box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#dropdown-list-combo-box-and-spin-box).

## 󠀁[purge](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#purge)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _clear, delete_, or 
_remove_.

See also [clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#clear),
[delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete), [remove](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#remove).

## 󠀁[push](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#push)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the act of pressing a button or a key on a keyboard. Instead,
use _press_.

See also [press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#press-press-and-hold).

## 󠀁[put](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#put)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _drag_.

Fr more information, see [Move, drag](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#move-drag).

## 󠀁[Python](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/?output_format=md#python)󠁿

Capitalize.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _Python
file_ rather than _.python file_ or _.py file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

---

## Q

# Q

## In this article

 * [quality](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quality)
 * [quick, quickly](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quick-quickly)
 * [quit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quit)
 * [quotation marks](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quotation-marks)
 * [quote](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quote)

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[quality](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quality)󠁿

Don’t use _quality_ by itself as an adjective. Instead, use a modifier and hyphenate.
For example, _high-quality, studio-quality_.

## 󠀁[quick, quickly](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quick-quickly)󠁿

Avoid using. _Quick_ or _quickly_ is a relative term, and in most cases, you can
express the same meaning of a sentence without using these terms.

## 󠀁[quit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quit)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the action of closing a program, window, or a connection. 
Instead use _close, stop_, or _end_.

See also [close](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#close),
[end](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#end), [exit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#exit),
[interrupt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#interrupt),
[stop](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#stop).

## 󠀁[quotation marks](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quotation-marks)󠁿

Not _quotes_ or _quote marks_. _Quote_ is a verb, and _quotation_ is an adjective
or a noun.

For more information, see [Quotation marks](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/quotation-marks/).

## 󠀁[quote](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/q/?output_format=md#quote)󠁿

Don’t use _quote_ to refer to cited content. Instead, use _quotation_.

 * [repo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#repo)
 * [reset](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#reset)

 * [restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#restart)
 * [restore](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#restore)
 * [required](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#required)
 * [right, rightmost, right-hand](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-rightmost-right-hand)
 * [right align, right-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-align-right-aligned)
 * [right justify, right-justified](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-justify-right-justified)
 * [robots.txt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#robots-txt)
 * [ROM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rom)
 * [Roman](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#roman)
 * [root, root directory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#root-root-directory)
 * [RSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rss)
 * [RTF](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rtf)
 * [RTL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rtl)
 * [run](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#run)
 * [runtime](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#runtime)

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[radio button](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#radio-button)󠁿

Use _radio button_ only in in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page
the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they
are doing. element. Refer to a radio button by its label. If you have to use a descriptor,
use _option_ or _option button_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[RAM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#ram)󠁿

Acronym for _random-access memory_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [memory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#memory).

## 󠀁[RDF](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rdf)󠁿

Initialism for _Resource Description Framework_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [RSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#rss).

## 󠀁[re-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#re)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _re-_ such as _reinstall_ and _reenter_
unless _re-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely necessary to avoid
confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[read-only](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#read-only)󠁿

Hyphenate.

## 󠀁[read/write](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#read-write)󠁿

Capitalize both _read_ and _write_ if _read_ is capitalized.

Not _read-write_.

## 󠀁[real time, real-time](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#real-time-real-time)󠁿

Two words. Hyphenate as an adjective.

## 󠀁[reboot](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#reboot)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead, use _restart_ and refer to the context of restarting the _device_.

See also [restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#restart).

## 󠀁[recommend](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#recommend)󠁿

Don’t use _we recommend_ or _WordPress recommends_. Instead, use _recommended_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** We recommend to use PHPPHP PHP (recursive acronym for PHP:
Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open source general-purpose scripting language
that is especially suited for web development and can be embedded into HTML. [https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php](https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php)
version 7.4 or greater.

 **Not recommended:** WordPress recommends to use PHPPHP PHP (recursive acronym 
for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open source general-purpose scripting
language that is especially suited for web development and can be embedded into 
HTML. [https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php](https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php)
version 7.4 or greater.

 **Recommended:** It’s recommended to use PHPPHP PHP (recursive acronym for PHP:
Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open source general-purpose scripting language
that is especially suited for web development and can be embedded into HTML. [https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php](https://www.php.net/manual/en/preface.php)
version 7.4 or greater.

 
 Don’t use _recommend_ when something is required.

See also [must](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#must), 
[should](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#should).

## 󠀁[reference](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#reference)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use _refer to_.

## 󠀁[refresh](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#refresh)󠁿

Use to describe updating a webpage.

Don’t use _refresh_ to describe an image being restored on the screen or data being
updated. Instead, use _update_.

See also [update](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#update).

## 󠀁[reinitialize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#reinitialize)󠁿

Don’t use to mean _restart_.

See also [initialize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#initialize),
[start, restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#start-restart).

## 󠀁[remote](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#remote)󠁿

It’s OK to use _remote_ as an adjective. Don’t use _remote_ as a verb.

## 󠀁[remove](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#remove)󠁿

It’s OK to use _remove_ as an verb. Don’t use to mean _delete_.

See also [clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#clear),
[delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete), [uninstall](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#uninstall),
[load](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#load).

## 󠀁[replace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#replace)󠁿

Don’t use as a noun.

See also [find and replace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#find-and-replace).

## 󠀁[repo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#repo)󠁿

Use _repository_ instead of _repo_ whenever possible.

## 󠀁[reset](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#reset)󠁿

Don’t use as a noun.

## 󠀁[REST API](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rest-api)󠁿

Abbreviation for _RESTful Application Program Interface_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[resolution](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#resolution)󠁿

Use a lowercase _x_ between the numerals in the dimensions, with no space between
the numerals and the x. You can also use the multiplication sign (×). Use a space
before and after the multiplication sign.

For more information, see [Dimensions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/numbers/#dimensions).

## 󠀁[restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#restart)󠁿

Use to describe closing and reopening a program or app or turning a device off and
then immediately back on. Refer to the context of restarting the _device_.

Don’t use as a noun.

See also [start, restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#start-restart).

## 󠀁[restore](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#restore)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe restoring an item or condition to its previous state.

Don’t use as a noun.

## 󠀁[required](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#required)󠁿

See [must](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#must).

## 󠀁[right, rightmost, right-hand](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-rightmost-right-hand)󠁿

Don’t use _right_ as a directional term by itself. Instead, use a term such as _upper
right, lower right, rightmost_, or _on the right side of_. When you use _right_ 
to modify a noun, insert a hyphen, as in _upper-right corner_.

Don’t use _right-hand_ as a modifier.

In general, avoid using directional language such as _left, right, up, down_ in 
instructions to locate UI elements or other content. Directional language proves
to be difficult for accessibility or for localization. People with cognitive impairments,
as well as people using assistive technologies such as screen-reading software and
might have difficulty interpreting directional language. If a particular UI element
or other content is difficult to convey, include a screenshot or illustration.

For more information, see [Procedures and instructions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/procedures/).

## 󠀁[right align, right-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-align-right-aligned)󠁿

Use to refer to text that’s aligned at the right margin. Hyphenate _right-aligned_.

Don’t use _right-justified_.

See also [justify, justified](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/j/#justify-justified),
[left align, left-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#left-align-left-aligned).

## 󠀁[right justify, right-justified](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-justify-right-justified)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _right-aligned_.

See also [right align, right-aligned](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#right-align-right-aligned).

## 󠀁[robots.txt](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#robots-txt)󠁿

Use code font.

For more information, see [Filenames](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/).

## 󠀁[ROM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rom)󠁿

Acronym for _read-only memory_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [memory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#memory).

## 󠀁[Roman](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#roman)󠁿

Don’t use to describe type that’s neither bold nor italic. Instead, use _regular
type_.

## 󠀁[root, root directory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#root-root-directory)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Use _root directory_,
not _home directory_

Describe the root of the file system by a leading slash (/).

## 󠀁[RSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rss)󠁿

Initialism for _Really Simple Syndication_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[RTF](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rtf)󠁿

Initialism for _Rich Text Format_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _RTF
file_ rather than _.rtf file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[RTL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#rtl)󠁿

Initialism for _right-to-left_. Use uppercase.

For more information, see [Writing documentation for a global audience](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/global-audience/).

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[run](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#run)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience.

## 󠀁[runtime](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/?output_format=md#runtime)󠁿

One word. Not _run time_ or _run-time_.

---
