## 󠀁[save](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#save)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe saving files to a device or storage device.

## 󠀁[screen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#screen)󠁿

Use _screen_ to refer to what the user looks at on a device.

Don’t use as a synonym for _display_.

See also [display](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#display).

## 󠀁[screenshot](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#screenshot)󠁿

One word. Not _screen shot_ or _screen-shot_.

See also [photo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#photo).

## 󠀁[screen resolution](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#screen-resolution)󠁿

See [resolution](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#resolution).

## 󠀁[scroll](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#scroll)󠁿

In user documentation, it’s OK to use _scroll_ to describe moving through pages,
documents, and other items instead of _drag_ or _swipe_.

Don’t use _scroll_ as a transitive verb.

## 󠀁[scroll bar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#scroll-bar)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page
the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they
are doing. element.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [scroll](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#scroll).

## 󠀁[SDK](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sdk)󠁿

Initialism for _Software Development Kit_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[search](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#search)󠁿

Use only as a verb, not as a noun or adjective.

## 󠀁[search and replace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#search-and-replace)󠁿

Don’t use to describe finding and replacing things in a document or page. Instead,
use _find and replace_.

See also [find and replace](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#find-and-replace).

## 󠀁[see](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#see)󠁿

OK to use when referring to links and cross-references.

For more information, see [Link text](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/linking/link-text/)
and [Cross-references](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/linking/cross-references/).

## 󠀁[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#select)󠁿

Use _select_ when referring to the action of the user selecting targets such as 
menu commands, checkboxes, items, and dropdown lists. _Select_ can be used interchangeably
instead of _click_ or _check_ in describing checkboxes and dropdown lists.

See also [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#select).

See also [clear](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#clear),
[click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#click), [double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-click-double-click),
[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-tap-double-tap),
[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold),
[tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[self-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#self)󠁿

In general, hyphenate words beginning with _self-_ such as _self-sufficient_ and
_self-explanatory_, unless _self-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely
necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[set](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#set)󠁿

Avoid using to describe user interactions with UI elements. Instead, use contextually
relevant verbs.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

## 󠀁[setup, set up](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#setup-set-up)󠁿

As a noun and an adjective, use _setup_ and as a verb use two words as in _set up_.

Don’t hyphenate.

## 󠀁[SFTP](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sftp)󠁿

Initialism for _Simple File Transfer Protocol_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use lowercase in developer documentation, such as commands.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[shaded](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shaded)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element.

Don’t use to describe a UI element such as a menu item, dropdown list option, or
button that the user can’t interact with due to certain conditions. Instead, use
_not available_ or _unavailable_. If you must describe their appearance, use _appears
dimmed_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [dimmed](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#dimmed),
[disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#disable-disabled),
[unavailable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#unavailable).

## 󠀁[shell](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shell)󠁿

OK to use as a noun in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid
using in user documentation and for a general audience.

Don’t use as a verb, such as _shell_ or _shell out_. Instead, use a contextually
relevant phrase, such as _create a new shell_.

## 󠀁[shortcut](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shortcut)󠁿

One word. Not _short cut_ or _short-cut_.

## 󠀁[should](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#should)󠁿

Use only when an action is recommended, but optional. Don’t use _should_ to indicate
probability. If you can’t make a definitive statement, use might or rephrase the
statement.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** You should back up your website regularly.

See also [must](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#must).

## 󠀁[shut down, shutdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shut-down-shutdown)󠁿

Use one word as a noun, and two words as a verb.

Use _shut down_ to describe exiting an operating system and turning off the device
in a single action.

Don’t use _shut down_ to describe turning off a device or as a synonym for _close_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

See also [turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off),
[shut down, shutdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shut-down-shutdown).

## 󠀁[sign in, sign-in, sign out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sign-in-sign-in-sign-out)󠁿

Hyphenate as a noun and adjective, as in _sign-in screen_. Use two words as a verb,
as in _sign in to your account_ and _sign out of your account_.

Use _sign in_ and _sign out_ to refer to start and end the procedure of starting
use of an internet account.

Use _sign in to_ and _sign out of_.

Don’t use _sign off, sign off of,_ or _sign off from_.

See also [login, log in, logout, log out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#login-log-in-logout-log-out),
[sign-on, sign](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sign-on-sign-on).

## 󠀁[sign-on, sign on](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sign-on-sign-on)󠁿

Hyphenate in in phrases such as _single sign-on_. Don’t hyphenate as a verb.

See also [sign in, sign-in, sign out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sign-in-sign-in-sign-out).

## 󠀁[simple, simply](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#simple-simply)󠁿

Avoid using. What might be simple for one person, may not be simple for others.

## 󠀁[site](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#site)󠁿

Use to describe a collection of webpages which are part of a bigger collective, 
such as the WordPress site. It’s OK to use _website_ instead of _site_ for clarity.

See also [page](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#page), 
[website](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/w/#website).

## 󠀁[sitemap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sitemap)󠁿

One word. Not _site map_ or _site-map_.

## 󠀁[since](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#since)󠁿

Don’t use as a synonym for _because_. _Since_ can be ambiguous and could refer to
time. _Because_ refers to a reason for something.

See [because](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/b/#because)

## 󠀁[size](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#size)󠁿

Avoid using size as a verb, as in _size the window_. Instead, use _change the size
of_ or _resize_.

## 󠀁[-size](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#size-2)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words ending with _size_ such as _medium-size_ and _letter-
size_

Not _-sized_.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[slave](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#slave)󠁿

Avoid using whenever possible.

See [master, master/slave](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#master-masterslave).

## 󠀁[sleep](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sleep)󠁿

Use to describe putting a device into a energy-saving state without shutting it 
down.

The computer _goes to sleep_, or the user can _put it to sleep_; the computer is
then _in sleep_ or _in sleep mode_. Don’t use the computer _is sleeping_ or the 
computer _is asleep_.

See also [shut down, shutdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shut-down-shutdown).

## 󠀁[slider](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#slider)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. Refer to an slider by its label. If you have to use
a descriptor, use _slider_.

In user documentation, it’s OK to use slider when you need to describe the UI element
used to set a value on a continuous range of possible values, such as screen brightness
or volume.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[SMTP](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#smtp)󠁿

Initialism for _Simple Mail Transfer Protocol_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use lowercase in developer documentation, such as protocols commands.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[sorry](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sorry)󠁿

Use _sorry_ only when the user is asked to do something inconvenient, the user can’t
use the product, the application or site is to blame for the situation, or when 
there is an issue with the product. It’s OK to use _sorry_ for other inconveniences
such as data loss, errors, application failure, or when the user has to get help
from a support representative.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** Sorry, the service is temporarily available.

See also [please](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#please).

## 󠀁[spam](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#spam)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb.

## 󠀁[spin box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#spin-box)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience.

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. Refer to a spin box by its label. If you have to use
a descriptor, use _spin box_ or _description box_.

For more information, see [Dropdown list, combo box, and spin box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#dropdown-list-combo-box-and-spin-box).

## 󠀁[smartphone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#smartphone)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _phone, mobile, mobile device,_ and _mobile phone_.

See also [mobile, mobile device, mobile phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#mobile-mobile-device-mobile-phone),
[phone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#phone).

## 󠀁[SQL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sql)󠁿

Initialism for _Structured Query Language_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use lowercase in developer documentation, such as commands.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [MySQL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#mysql).

## 󠀁[SSH](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#ssh)󠁿

Initialism for _Secure Shell_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use lowercase in developer documentation, such as protocols or commands.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

Don’t use _ssh_ or _SSHSSH Secure SHell – a protocol for securely connecting to 
a remote system in addition to or in place of a password._ as a verb.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** SSHSSH Secure SHell – a protocol for securely connecting to
a remote system in addition to or in place of a password. into your remote shell.

 **Recommended:** Use `ssh` to connect to your remote shell.

## 󠀁[SSL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#ssl)󠁿

Initialism for _Secure Socket Layer_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[standalone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#standalone)󠁿

It’s OK to use _standalone_ as an adjective. Don’t use as a noun.

## 󠀁[start, restart](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#start-restart)󠁿

Don’t use _start_ to describe selecting a program or app to open it. Instead, use
_open_.

Use _restart_ to describe closing and reopening a program or app or turning a device
off and then immediately back on.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

See also [turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#turn-on-turn-off),
[shut down, shutdown](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#shut-down-shutdown).

## 󠀁[status bar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#status-bar)󠁿

In general, emphasize on the task to be accomplished, rather than how the user should
interact with the UI element. Refer to a status bar by its label. If you have to
use a descriptor, use _status bar_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#menu-bar).

## 󠀁[stop, stop responding](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#stop-stop-responding)󠁿

Don’t use _stop_ to mean _exit a program or application_.

Use _stop responding_ when a program encounters a problem and can’t close itself.
Use _close_ to describe the action a program takes to close itself when it has encountered
a problem and can’t continue.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#interaction-verbs).

## 󠀁[storage, storage device](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#storage-storage-device)󠁿

Don’t use _storage_ to refer to available space on a disk. Instead, use _storage
space_ or _disk space_.

Use _storage device_ instead of _disk_ to refer generally to external drives such
as hard drives, solid-state drives, flash storage, and other types of storage hardware.

See also [memory](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/m/#memory).

## 󠀁[style sheet](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#style-sheet)󠁿

Two words. Not _stylesheet_ or _style-sheet_.

This is the official spelling, per the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).

See also [CSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#css).

## 󠀁[sub-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sub)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _sub-_ such as _subsection, subheading,_
and _subdirectory_, unless _sub-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely
necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[subclass](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#subclass)󠁿

One word. Not _sub class_ or _sub-class_.

Don’t use as a verb. Instead, use _create a subclass_ or a similar contextual verb.

## 󠀁[subnet](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#subnet)󠁿

One word. Not _sub net_ or _sub-net_.

Shortened abbreviation of _subnetwork_. Be consistent in using one or the other 
in a single document.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[such as](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#such-as)󠁿

It’s OK to use _such as_ or _like_ for comparisons or examples.

See also [like](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#like).

## 󠀁[super-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#super)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _super-_ such as _supercomputer_
and _supercritical_, unless _super-_ is followed by a proper noun or it is absolutely
necessary to avoid confusion.

For more information, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[surf](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#surf)󠁿

Avoid using _surf_ to refer to the action of browsing.

## 󠀁[SVG](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#svg)󠁿

Acronym for _Scalable Vector Graphics_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _SVG
file_ rather than _.svg file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[SVN](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#svn)󠁿

Shortened abbreviation for _Subversion_. Use uppercase.

It’s OK to use lowercase in developer documentation, such as commands.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[swipe](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#swipe)󠁿

When the environment is presumably a touch surface or device, use _swipe_ to describe
a short, quick movement in the direction opposite to the way the page scrolls. Include
the direction of the swipe—up, down, left, or right—if it’s needed to describe the
action.

See also [flick](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/f/#flick).

## 󠀁[switch](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#switch)󠁿

As a verb, use instead of _activate_ or _toggle_.

OK to use as a noun as in _toggle button_.

For more information, see [Toggle button](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#toggle-button).

See also [toggle](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/#toggle).

## 󠀁[symbol](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#symbol)󠁿

Don’t use _symbol_ when you mean _button_ or _icon_. A user can interact with a 
_button_ or _icon_ but cannot interact with a _symbol_.

It’s OK to use _symbol_ to refer to text characters, as in the percent symbol (%).
Don’t use _symbol_ when you mean _character, letter_, or _digit_.

Use _sign_, not _symbol_, in the following terms: _division sign, equal sign, greater-
than sign, less-than sign, minus sign, multiplication sign, number sign_, and _plus
sign_.

When referring to a sign or symbol, introduce its spelled-out version and then the
sign or symbol in parentheses. It’s acceptable to use a symbol by itself in UI, 
tables, or headings where space is limited.

For more information, see [Parentheses](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/parentheses/)
and [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

Write out the plurals of symbols, showing the use in parentheses. Don’t add _s_ 
or _‘s_ to a symbol.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Enter two backslashes (\s) in the terminal.

 **Not recommended:** Enter two backslashes (\’s) in the terminal.

 **Recommended:** Enter two backslashes (\) in the terminal.

See also [button](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/b/#button),
[icon](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/i/#icon).

## 󠀁[sync](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#sync)󠁿

Shortened term for _synchronize_. Not _synch, synching,_ or _synched_.

OK to use as a noun or an adjective.

Use _sync with_ not _sync from_ or _sync to_.

## 󠀁[Syndication](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#syndication)󠁿

See [RSS](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#rss).

## 󠀁[system](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/?output_format=md#system)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to a _computer_ by itself.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Turn on your system.

 **Recommended:** Turn on your computer.

---

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[tab](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tab)󠁿

Don’t use as a verb.

As a noun, use to refer to tabs that show a separate view or subpages on a webpage,
dialog box, browser, or menu. For other uses of the term, clarify the meaning with
a descriptor, such as _the Tab key, a tab character, a tab stop_, or _a tab mark
on the ruler_.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[tablet](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tablet)󠁿

OK to use. If you are unable to distinguish between a _tablet_ and a _laptop_ or
_phone_, use _device_.

## 󠀁[tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tap-double-tap)󠁿

Use _tap_ to describe selecting, opening, or enabling targets such as buttons, links,
list items, or other elements with a finger or pen by tapping it once. Don’t use
_tap on_.

Use _double-tap_ to describe selecting, opening, or enabling targets such as buttons,
links, list items, or other elements with a finger or pen by tapping it twice in
quick succession. Hyphenate _double-tap_. Don’t use _double-tap_ on.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#tap).

See also [click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/c/#click),
[double click, double-click](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-click-double-click),
[double tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#double-tap-double-tap),
[press, press and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/p/#press-press-and-hold),
[select](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#select), [touch and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch-and-hold).

## 󠀁[tap and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tap-and-hold)󠁿

Don’t use. _Tap_ describes touching and releasing quickly Instead, use [touch and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch-and-hold).

See also [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tap-double-tap),
[touch and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch-and-hold).

## 󠀁[tarball](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tarball)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use [tar file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tar-file).

## 󠀁[tar file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tar-file)󠁿

Acronym for _Tape Archive_ file.

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _tar
file_ rather than _.tar file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[target](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#target)󠁿

Don’t use, especially in reference to people. Instead, use _intended for, looking
for, focused on_, and _interacting with_. Instead of using _target file_, refer 
to the specific file or folder, or use _destination file_ or _destination folder_.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Move the files to the target folder.

 **Recommended:** Move the files to the `wp-contents` folder.

## 󠀁[taskbar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#taskbar)󠁿

One word. Not _task bar_ or _task-bar_.

## 󠀁[TB, terabyte](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tb-terabyte)󠁿

Initialism for _terabyte_. Use uppercase.

One _TB_ equals 1000^(4) bytes in the context of file size or storage capacity, 
and 1024^(4) bytes in the context of computer memory.

In the noun form, insert a space between the numeral and the abbreviation. Use the
preposition _of_ before the unit.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 2 TB of storage

Don’t hyphenate the adjective form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** a 2 TB SSD

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[Tbit, terabit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tbit-terabit)󠁿

Initialism for _terabit_.

One _Tbit_ equals 1000^(4) bits in the context of file size or storage capacity,
and 1024^(4) bits in the context of computer memory.

In the noun form, insert a space between the numeral and the abbreviation. Use the
preposition _of_ before the unit.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 10 TBit of memory

Don’t hyphenate the adjective form.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** 10 TBit switch

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[Tbps (Tbit/s), terabits per second](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tbps-tbit-s-terabits-per-second)󠁿

Abbreviation for _terabits per second_.

For more information, see [Units of measurement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/units-of-measurement/).

See also [Tbit, terabit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tbit-terabit).

## 󠀁[TBps (TB/s), terabytes per second](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tbps-tb-s-terabytes-per-second)󠁿

Abbreviation for _terabytes per second_.

For more information, see [Units of measurement](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/units-of-measurement/).

See also [TB, terabyte](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tb-terabyte).

## 󠀁[TCP/IP](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tcp-ip)󠁿

Initialism for _Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[terminate](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#terminate)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Don’t use as 
a synonym for _close_ or _exit_.

## 󠀁[text box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#text-box)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, refer to the box by its UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface–
the layout of the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ 
and less about what they are doing. label or use _box_.

For more information, see [Text box](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#text-box).

## 󠀁[text file](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#text-file)󠁿

Don’t use a filename extension to refer to a type of file. For example, use _text
file_ rather than _.txt file_.

For more information, see [Referring to file types](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/filenames/#referring-to-file-types).

## 󠀁[that](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#that)󠁿

Use to introduce a restrictive or defining clause; clauses beginning with _that_
are generally not set off with commas.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** GutenbergGutenberg The Gutenberg project is the new Editor Interface
for WordPress. The editor improves the process and experience of creating new content,
making writing rich content much simpler. It uses ‘blocks’ to add richness rather
than shortcodes, custom HTML etc. [https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/](https://wordpress.org/gutenberg/)
is the latest blockBlock Block is the abstract term used to describe units of markup
that, composed together, form the content or layout of a webpage using the WordPress
editor. The idea combines concepts of what in the past may have achieved with shortcodes,
custom HTML, and embed discovery into a single consistent API and user experience.
editor that is widely used.

Insert a noun after _that_ for clarity, whenever possible. It is acceptable to omit
the noun in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited. If you aren’t sure what
noun _that_ refers to, then consider rephrasing.

See also [which](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/w/#which).

## 󠀁[they, their, them](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#they-their-them)󠁿

Use _they, their, them_ as gender-neutral pronouns when referring to people of unspecified
gender. Don’t use _he, him, she, her,_ or renditions like _s/he, he/she,_ or _(s)
he_ for people of unspecified gender.

For more information, see [Pronouns and gender](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/pronouns/#pronouns-and-genders)
and [Writing about genders](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/inclusivity/).

## 󠀁[third party](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#third-party)󠁿

Hyphenate as adjectives.

## 󠀁[this, that](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#this-that)󠁿

Insert a noun after _this_ for clarity, whenever possible. It is acceptable to omit
the noun in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited. If you aren’t sure what
noun _this_ refers to, then consider rephrasing.

## 󠀁[thousand, K](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#thousand-k)󠁿

Don’t abbreviate _thousand_ as _K_ or _k_. Spell out the word or denote the entire
number.

For more information, see [Abbreviations in numbers](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/numbers/#abbreviations).

## 󠀁[three-dimensional](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#three-dimensional)󠁿

See [3D](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/numbers/#3d).

## 󠀁[thru](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#thru)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _through_.

## 󠀁[timeframe](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#timeframe)󠁿

Avoid using. Not _time frame_. Instead, use _period, schedule, deadline_, or _when_.

## 󠀁[timeline](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#timeline)󠁿

One word. Not _time line_ or _time-line_.

## 󠀁[timeout, time out](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#timeout-time-out)󠁿

Don’t hyphenate and insert a space as an adjective or a noun. Don’t hyphenate as
a verb phrase such as _the connection timed out_.

## 󠀁[timestamp](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#timestamp)󠁿

One word. Not _time stamp_ or _time-stamp_.

## 󠀁[time to live, TTL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#time-to-live-ttl)󠁿

Not _time-to-live_. Abbreviate as _TTL_ after first use.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[time zone, time-zone](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#time-zone-time-zone)󠁿

Two words. Not _timezone_.

Don’t hyphenate and insert a space as a noun. Hyphenate as an adjective.

## 󠀁[tl;dr](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tldr)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use something like _To summarize_, or rewrite and rephrase the
sentence.

## 󠀁[toggle](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#toggle)󠁿

As a verb, it is OK to use _toggle_ in developer documentation and for a technical
audience. Avoid using in user documentation and for a general audience; instead 
use _turn on or turn off, switch between, enable_, or relevant terminology depending
on the context.

OK to use as a noun or an adjective, as in _toggle button_ or _toggle switch_. A
_toggle button_ is a UI element that switches back and forth between on and off 
options or states.

For more information, see [Toggle button](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#toggle-button)
and [Formatting UI element names](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#formatting-ui-element-names).

## 󠀁[tool](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tool)󠁿

Use _tool_, not _utility_, to describe a function or feature that helps users complete
tasks.

## 󠀁[toolbar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#toolbar)󠁿

One word. Not _tool bar_ or _tool-bar_.

## 󠀁[toolkit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#toolkit)󠁿

One word. Not _tool kit_ or _tool-kit_.

## 󠀁[top left, top right](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#top-left-top-right)󠁿

Don’t use.

See [upper left, upper right](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/#upper-left-upper-right).

## 󠀁[touch](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _tap_. However, _touch and hold_ is OK to use.

See [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tap-double-tap),
[touch and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch-and-hold).

## 󠀁[touch and hold](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touch-and-hold)󠁿

When the environment is presumably a touch device, use _touch and hold_ to describe
selecting, opening, or enabling targets such as buttons, links, list items, or other
elements with a finger or pen by tapping and holding it stationary until a result
occurs. Don’t use _touch and hold on_.

Don’t use _tap and hold_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#select-and-hold).

See also [tap, double-tap](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tap-double-tap).

## 󠀁[touchscreen](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#touchscreen)󠁿

One word. Not _touch screen_ or _touch-screen_.

## 󠀁[toward](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#toward)󠁿

Not _towards_.

## 󠀁[trackball](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#trackball)󠁿

One word. Not _track ball_ or _track-ball_.

## 󠀁[trackpad](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#trackpad)󠁿

One word. Not _track pad_ or _track-pad_.

## 󠀁[traditional](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#traditional)󠁿

Avoid using; instead, use a detailed and accurate term whenever possible.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Traditionally, pages also do not make use of categories and
tags like posts do.

 **Recommended:** Conventionally, pages also do not make use of categories and tags
like posts do.

 **Not recommended:** If you want to use the theme for a traditional blog, the centered
content column and considered typography makes it perfect for that as well.

 **Recommended:** If you want to use the theme for a straightforward blog, the centered
content column and considered typography makes it perfect for that as well.

 **Not recommended:** Unlike a traditional system cron that schedules tasks for 
specific times, WP-Cron uses intervals to simulate a system cron.

 **Recommended:** Unlike a system cron that schedules tasks for specific times (
e.g. “every hour at 5 minutes past the hour”), WP-Cron uses intervals to simulate
a system cron.

## 󠀁[trojan](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#trojan)󠁿

OK to use.

## 󠀁[troubleshoot](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#troubleshoot)󠁿

One word. Not _trouble shoot_ or _trouble-shoot_.

## 󠀁[turn on, turn off](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#turn-on-turn-off)󠁿

Use to describe turning a device on or off. Don’t use _power on/power off_ or _start/
stop_.

OK to use when referring to the action of turning a switch or toggle key on or off.

For more information, see [Switch, turn on, turn off, enable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#switch-turn-on-turn-off-enable).

See also [enable, enabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#enable-enabled),
[disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#disable-disabled).

## 󠀁[tutorial](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#tutorial)󠁿

OK to use.

For more information, see [Procedures](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/procedures/).

## 󠀁[two-dimensional](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#two-dimensional)󠁿

See [2D](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/numbers/#2d).

## 󠀁[type](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#type)󠁿

OK to use.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#enter-type-input).

See also [enter](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/e/#enter).

## 󠀁[typically](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/t/?output_format=md#typically)󠁿

Use to describe something that is standard or expected under normal circumstances.
Avoid using as the first word of a sentence, as the meaning of the content can be
misunderstood.

---

## 󠀁[UI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#ui)󠁿

Initialism for _User Interface_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use _UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page the
user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they are
doing._ to generically refer to UI elements. Instead, use the specific UI element
term.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** In the **Link** UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface –
the layout of the page the user interacts with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ 
and less about what they are doing., enter your sitemap link.

 **Recommended:** In the **Link** box, enter your sitemap link.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[UK](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uk)󠁿

Initialism for _United Kingdom_. Use uppercase.

Don’t use as a synonym for _Great Britain (GB)_ or _England_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[un-](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#un)󠁿

In general, don’t hyphenate words beginning with _un-_ such as _unable_ and _undo_,
unless absolutely necessary, to avoid confusion. For example, hyphenate in cases
such as _un-fitting_, or where _un-_ is followed by a proper noun such as _un-American_.

For more information about hyphenation, see [Hyphens](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/punctuation/hyphens/).

For word usage of specific terms, see [The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/).

## 󠀁[unarchive](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unarchive)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _extract_.

## 󠀁[unavailable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unavailable)󠁿

Use to describe a UI element such as a menu item, dropdown list option, or button
that the user can’t interact with due to certain conditions. Also, use _unavailable_
to describe the unavailability of a product or service.

In general, describe how the user should interact with the UI rather than describing
the state of the UI. Use _appears dimmed_ for describing its appearance. Also include
how the user can enable it and interact with the element.

**Examples**

 **Recommended:** If the editor permissions are unavailable, contact your site administrator.

 **Recommended:** The **Update** button is unavailable unless you change the post
contents.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [dimmed](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#dimmed),
[disable, disabled](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#disable-disabled),
[shaded](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/s/#shaded).

## 󠀁[uncheck](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uncheck)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the action of clearing a check mark from a checkbox. Instead,
use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Uncheck the **Crop thumbnail** checkbox.

 **Recommended:** Clear the **Crop thumbnail** checkbox.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[unclick](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unclick)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[uncompress](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uncompress)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _extract_.

## 󠀁[undelete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#undelete)󠁿

Don’t use.

See [restore](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#restore).

## 󠀁[undeploy](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#undeploy)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _remove_ or _withdraw_.

## 󠀁[under](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#under)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to item menus or other UI elements.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** Under the **Text** menu, select **Encoding**.

 **Recommended:** In the **Text** menu, select **Encoding**.

## 󠀁[underline, underscore](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#underline-underscore)󠁿

Use _underline_ to describe text formatting that puts a line under the characters.
Use _underscore_ to refer to the underscore character ( _ ).

## 󠀁[undo](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#undo)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe undoing any particular action.

Don’t use _undo_ as a noun.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** After an undo, you can redo by pressing press Ctrl+Y.

 **Recommended:** After undoing an action, you can redo by pressing press Ctrl+Y.

## 󠀁[unhighlight](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unhighlight)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

## 󠀁[uninstall](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uninstall)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe the action of removing programs, apps, other software,
and hardware from a device.

Don’t use _uninstall_ as a noun.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** After the uninstall of the program, restart your computer.

 **Recommended:** After uninstalling the program, restart your computer.

See also [delete](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#delete),
[remove](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/r/#remove).

## 󠀁[UNIX](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unix)󠁿

No spelled-out term. Use uppercase.

## 󠀁[UNIX epoch time](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unix-epoch-time)󠁿

Use rather than _UNIX time_ or _epoch time_ to refer to a point in time represented
as a number of seconds since the UNIX epoch (00:00:00 UTC on January 1, 1970), ignoring
leap seconds.

## 󠀁[unmark](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unmark)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the action of clearing a check mark from a checkbox. Instead,
use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [uncheck](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uncheck).

## 󠀁[unmount](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unmount)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe the action of making a disk or disk image unavailable.

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _eject_.

## 󠀁[unselect](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unselect)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the action of clearing a check mark from a checkbox. Instead,
use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [uncheck](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uncheck).

## 󠀁[unset](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unset)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _clear_ for checkboxes, and _deselect_ for other UI elements.

For more information, see [UI elements](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/).

See also [uncheck](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uncheck).

## 󠀁[untar](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#untar)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _extract_.

## 󠀁[unzip](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#unzip)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _extract_.

## 󠀁[update](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#update)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe installing a version of a product with a newer, _minor_
version of the same product, but not upgrading it to then next _major_ version. 
Use as a noun to describe the process of updating software.

Not _up-date_ or _up date_.

Don’t use _update_ as a synonym for _upgrade_.

See also [upgrade](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upgrade).

## 󠀁[upgradable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upgradable)󠁿

Not _upgradeable_.

## 󠀁[upgrade](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upgrade)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe replacing an installed version of a product with a newer,
_major_ version of the same product. Use as a noun to describe the process of upgrading
software.

Not _up-grade_ or _up grade_.

Don’t use _upgrade_ as a synonym for _update_. Do not use to mean _migrate_ or _port_.

See also [update](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#update).

## 󠀁[upload](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upload)󠁿

Use as a verb to describe the action of transferring files from a local device to
a website, server, or to the cloud.

Describe what the customer is transferring _and_ where the customer is transferring
it _to_. In grammatical terms, use both a subject (the thing to be uploaded) and
an object (the thing the subject is uploaded to) with the verb _upload_.

See also [download](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#download),
[load](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/l/#load).

## 󠀁[uppercase](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uppercase)󠁿

One word. Not _upper case_ or _upper-case_. Don’t use _uppercase_ as a verb. Don’t
use _uppercased_.

When using both _uppercase_ and _lowercase_ together as a noun or to modify a noun,
spell out both words. Don’t use a suspended hyphen (as in _upper- and lowercase_).

## 󠀁[upper left, upper right](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upper-left-upper-right)󠁿

Hyphenate as adjectives. Use instead of _top left_ and _top right_.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** The upper-left corner

In general, avoid using directional language such as _left, right, up, down_ in 
instructions to locate UI elements or other content. Directional language proves
to be difficult for accessibility or for localization. People with cognitive impairments,
as well as people using assistive technologies such as screen-reading software might
have difficulty interpreting directional language. If a particular UI element or
other content is difficult to convey, include a screenshot or illustration.

For more information, see [Writing documentation for an international audience](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/general-guidelines/global-audience/)
and [Procedures and instructions](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/formatting/procedures/).

## 󠀁[upsize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upsize)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead, use _scale up_.

## 󠀁[uptime](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uptime)󠁿

One word. Not _up time_ or _up-time_.

## 󠀁[upward](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#upward)󠁿

Not _upwards_.

## 󠀁[URI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#uri)󠁿

Initialism for _Uniform Resource Identifier_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[URL](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#url)󠁿

Initialism for _Uniform Resource Locator_. Use uppercase. Plural is _URLs_.

Write _a URL_ instead of _an URL_, as the most common pronunciation starts with 
a consonant sound. For more information, see [Articles](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/articles/).

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

For more information about styling and formatting URLs, see the [Linking section](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/linking/).

## 󠀁[US](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#us)󠁿

Initialism for _United States_. OK to use as an abbreviation for _United States_.
Use uppercase.

Not _U.S., U.S.A._, or _USA_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[usable](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#usable)󠁿

Not _useable_.

## 󠀁[USB](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#usb)󠁿

Initialism for _Universal Serial Bus_. Use uppercase.

Don’t spell out. Use only as an adjective.

**Example**

 **Recommended:** USB drive

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[user](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#user)󠁿

Use _you_ when addressing the reader instead of _user_. If your documentation audience
consists of users, avoid using this term. It is OK to use _user_ in developer documentation
and for a technical audience.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** The user can click the **Save** button to save changes.

 **Recommended:** You can click the **Save** button to save changes.

For more information, see [Grammatical person](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/grammatical-person/).

## 󠀁[user base](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#user-base)󠁿

Two words. Not _userbase_.

## 󠀁[user interface](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#user-interface)󠁿

See [UI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#ui).

## 󠀁[username](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#username)󠁿

One word. Not _user name_ or _user-name_.

## 󠀁[UTF](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#utf)󠁿

Initialism for _Unicode Transformation Format_. Use uppercase.

Include the hyphen in the names of Unicode encodings, such as _UTF-8, UTF-16_, and
_UTF-32_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[utility](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#utility)󠁿

Don’t use.

## 󠀁[utilize, utilization](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#utilize-utilization)󠁿

Use with caution. Don’t use _utilize_ when you mean _use_. It’s OK to use _utilize_
or _utilization_ when referring to the quantity of a resource being used.

**Examples**

 **Not recommended:** To select a template to display the page, utilize the query
string.

 **Recommended:** To select a template to display the page, use the query string.

 **Recommended:** The program will resume execution when the CPU utilization falls
under 90%.

## 󠀁[UX](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#ux)󠁿

Initialism for _User Experience_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

See also [UI](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/u/?output_format=md#ui).

---

<span id="v-page-99"></span>
## V

**Source:** https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/

# V

## In this article

 * [version, v.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#version-v)
 * [versus, vs., v.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#versus-vs-v)
 * [very](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#very)
 * [via](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#via)
 * [vice versa](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vice-versa)
 * [video card](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-card)
 * [video display](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-display)
 * [video driver](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-driver)
 * [virtual](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtual)
 * [virtualize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtualize)
 * [virtual machine, VM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtual-machine-vm)
 * [visit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#visit)
 * [volume (disk)](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#volume-disk)
 * [VPN](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vpn)
 * [VVV](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vvv)

[↑ Back to top](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#wp--skip-link--target)

## 󠀁[version, v.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#version-v)󠁿

Use lowercase when using _v_ or _v._ for indicating a version.

Don’t use _version_ as a verb such as _versioning_.

## 󠀁[versus, vs., v.](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#versus-vs-v)󠁿

Avoid using _vs._ or _v._ as an abbreviation for _versus_. Acceptable to use in 
UIUI UI is an acronym for User Interface – the layout of the page the user interacts
with. Think ‘how are they doing that’ and less about what they are doing., tables,
or headings where space is limited. Instead, use the unabbreviated term _versus_
or other relevant phrasing such as _compared to_.

## 󠀁[very](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#very)󠁿

Avoid using.

## 󠀁[via](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#via)󠁿

Avoid using. Instead use _by, from, through, using_, or _with_. Acceptable to use
in UI, tables, or headings where space is limited.

## 󠀁[vice versa](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vice-versa)󠁿

Don’t use. Instead use _conversely, otherwise, the other way round,_ or _on the 
contrary_.

In some contexts, _vice versa_ is confusing or ambiguous in determining which two
opposite things are swapped with each other. In such cases, describe what two things
are swapped without ambiguity.

## 󠀁[video card](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-card)󠁿

Use _video card_ instead of _video adapter, display adapter, graphics adapter, graphics
card_, or _graphics board_.

## 󠀁[video display](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-display)󠁿

Don’t use.

## 󠀁[video driver](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#video-driver)󠁿

Use _video driver_ instead of _display driver_ or _graphics driver_.

## 󠀁[virtual](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtual)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience.

Use only to refer to a device or service that doesn’t physically exist or appears
to be something it’s not. For example, a _virtual machine (VM)_ isn’t an actual 
machine; it’s a machine that emulates a real computer.

## 󠀁[virtualize](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtualize)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience.

## 󠀁[virtual machine, VM](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#virtual-machine-vm)󠁿

Use _virtual machine_ when introducing the term for the first time. On subsequent
mentions, it is OK to use _VM_ or _VM instance_.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[visit](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#visit)󠁿

Don’t use to refer to the action of opening a website or webpage. Instead, use _go
to_.

For more information, see [Interaction verbs](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/developer-content/ui-elements/#go-to).

## 󠀁[volume (disk)](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#volume-disk)󠁿

OK to use in developer documentation and for a technical audience. Avoid using in
user documentation and for a general audience; instead, use _disk_.

To refer to storage that may include different types of disks, just use _disk_. 
You can also refer to a specific type of disk such as _solid-state drive, hard-disk,_
or _flash storage_.

See also [disk](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/d/#disk).

## 󠀁[VPN](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vpn)󠁿

Initialism for _Virtual Private Network_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

## 󠀁[VVV](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/word-list/v/?output_format=md#vvv)󠁿

Initialism for _Varying Vagrant Vagrants_. Use uppercase.

For more information about spelling out abbreviations, see [Abbreviations](https://make.wordpress.org/docs/style-guide/language-grammar/abbreviations/).

---
